alfiyya.f: Does it also apply before the extended alif in «سكران» and similar forms?
alfiyya.b: Yes, the preceding letter is fatḥa before the extended alif.

ar.f: هل يجري الفتح قبل مد سكران وما ألحق به؟
ar.b: نعم، يفتح ما قبل مد «سكران» وما ألحق به.

alfiyya.f: How are feminine alif and tāʾ treated in diminutive patterning?
alfiyya.b: Treat the feminine alif and tāʾ as separate from the base of the noun.

ar.f: كيف تعامل ألف التأنيث وتاؤها في بنية التصغير؟
ar.b: تعد ألف التأنيث وتاؤها منفصلتين عن أصل البنية.

alfiyya.f: Which other endings are treated as separate in diminutive formation?
alfiyya.b: The nisba ending, and the second component of an annexed or compound expression.

ar.f: ما الزيادات الأخرى التي تعد منفصلة في التصغير؟
ar.b: تُعد منفصلة ياء النسب وعجز المضاف والمركب.

alfiyya.f: How are the extra letters of «فَعْلان» treated when four or more letters precede them?
alfiyya.b: They are treated as separate, as in «زعفران».

ar.f: كيف تعامل زيادتا فعلان إذا تقدمهما أربعة أحرف فأكثر؟
ar.b: تعدّان منفصلتين، مثل «زعفران».

alfiyya.f: How are dual and sound-plural endings treated in diminutive formation?
alfiyya.b: Treat them as separate endings rather than part of the base.

ar.f: كيف تعامل علامة التثنية والجمع السالم في التصغير؟
ar.b: يُقدّر انفصال ما دلّ على التثنية أو الجمع السالم.

alfiyya.f: What happens to short feminine alif in a diminutive when the word has more than four letters?
alfiyya.b: It does not remain as part of the diminutive.
alfiyya.s: Bayt 844 — ألف التأنيث المقصورة في التصغير

ar.f: ماذا يحدث لألف التأنيث المقصورة إذا زاد الاسم على أربعة أحرف؟
ar.b: لا تثبت ألف التأنيث المقصورة في هذه الحالة.

alfiyya.f: What two diminutive forms are given for «حبارى»?
alfiyya.b: «الحُبَيْرَى» and «الحُبَيِّر».

ar.f: ما وجها تصغير حبارى؟
ar.b: «الحُبَيْرَى» و«الحُبَيِّر».

alfiyya.f: When a weak second radical was changed from its original form, what is done in the diminutive?
alfiyya.b: Restore the original radical, as «قيمة» → «قُوَيْمة».

ar.f: ماذا يفعل في التصغير إذا كانت العين اللينة مقلوبة عن أصل؟
ar.b: تُردّ إلى أصلها، مثل «قيمة» ← «قُوَيْمة».

alfiyya.f: What is the diminutive of «عيد» and its status?
alfiyya.b: «عُيَيْد» is anomalous.

ar.f: ما تصغير عيد، وما حكمه؟
ar.b: «عُيَيْد» شاذ.

alfiyya.f: What rule applies to plural formation in relation to diminutive patterns?
alfiyya.b: Plural formation follows the patterns known from diminutive formation, according to the poem’s rule.

ar.f: ما علاقة الجمع بأحكام التصغير؟
ar.b: يُراعى في الجمع ما عُرف من أحكام التصغير.

alfiyya.f: How is a second extra alif treated in a diminutive?
alfiyya.b: Change it to wāw; do the same if its original identity is unknown.

ar.f: كيف تعامل الألف الزائدة الثانية في التصغير؟
ar.b: تُقلب واواً، وكذلك إن جُهل أصلها.

alfiyya.f: When is a defective noun completed in the diminutive?
alfiyya.b: Complete it unless its third position contains something other than tāʾ, as in «ما».

ar.f: متى يُتمّ الاسم المنقوص عند التصغير؟
ar.b: يُتمّ ما لم يكن في ثالثه غير التاء، مثل «ما».

alfiyya.f: How does a diminutive formed from a shortened name (tarḫīm) work?
alfiyya.b: It may use the original form as its base, as «العُطيف» from «المعطف».

ar.f: كيف يصاغ التصغير من الاسم المرخّم؟
ar.b: يكتفى بالأصل، مثل «العُطيف» من «المعطف».

alfiyya.f: What ending is added when diminishing a bare three-letter feminine noun?
alfiyya.b: Add feminine tāʾ, as with a feminine «سِنّ».

ar.f: ماذا يزاد عند تصغير مؤنث ثلاثي مجرد؟
ar.b: تختم بالتاء، مثل «سِنّة».

alfiyya.f: When is that feminine tāʾ not added?
alfiyya.b: When adding it would create ambiguity, as in «شجر، بقر، خمس».

ar.f: متى لا تزاد تاء التصغير للمؤنث؟
ar.b: إذا أوجبت لبساً، مثل «شجر» و«بقر» و«خمس».

alfiyya.f: Can the tāʾ be omitted even where there is no ambiguity?
alfiyya.b: Yes, omission without ambiguity is anomalous.

ar.f: هل تحذف التاء أحياناً من غير لبس؟
ar.b: نعم، وقد شذّ تركها مع عدم اللبس.

alfiyya.f: Can tāʾ be added to a common triliteral noun in the diminutive?
alfiyya.b: It is rare.

ar.f: هل تلحق التاء اسماً ثلاثياً كثير الاستعمال في التصغير؟
ar.b: نادر.

alfiyya.f: Are demonstratives and relative pronouns diminished?
alfiyya.b: Some are exceptionally diminished, including «الذي، التي، ذا» and their forms «تا، تي».

ar.f: هل تصغر أسماء الإشارة والموصولات؟
ar.b: صُغّرت شذوذاً ألفاظ مثل «الذي» و«التي» و«ذا» وفروعها «تا» و«تي».

alfiyya.f: What is nisba (relational adjective formation)?
alfiyya.b: It is forming an adjective of affiliation by adding yāʾ with a preceding kasra, as in «كرسيّ».

ar.f: ما النسب؟
ar.b: النسب إلحاق ياء مشددة مكسور ما قبلها للدلالة على الانتماء، مثل «كرسيّ».

alfiyya.f: What happens to the ending after the nisba yāʾ?
alfiyya.b: Its preceding consonant receives kasra.
alfiyya.s: Bayt 855 — كسر ما قبل ياء النسب

ar.f: ما حكم الحرف الذي يلي ياء النسب؟
ar.b: يجب كسر ما قبل ياء النسب.

alfiyya.f: What happens to other endings contained in a word when forming nisba?
alfiyya.b: Delete them; do not retain feminine tāʾ or its extended-alif ending.

ar.f: ماذا يفعل ببقية الزوائد عند النسب؟
ar.b: تُحذف الزيادات الأخرى، ولا تثبت تاء التأنيث ولا مدّها.

alfiyya.f: How is a fourth-letter alif preceded by a sākin second radical handled in nisba?
alfiyya.b: It may be changed to wāw or deleted.

ar.f: كيف تعامل الألف رابعة إذا سبقها ساكن؟
ar.b: يجوز قلبها واواً أو حذفها.

alfiyya.f: Why can a fourth-letter alif be changed or deleted?
alfiyya.b: It may resemble an augment or an original radical; if it is original, changing it is the preferred treatment.

ar.f: ما علة قلب الألف الرابعة أو حذفها؟
ar.b: لشبهها بالزائد والأصلي؛ والقلب هو المختار في الأصلية.

alfiyya.f: What happens to an optional alif in nisba formation?
alfiyya.b: Delete it.

ar.f: ماذا يفعل بالألف الجائزة في النسب؟
ar.b: تُحذف.

alfiyya.f: What happens to the yāʾ of a defective noun when it is fifth radical?
alfiyya.b: Delete it.

ar.f: ماذا يفعل بياء المنقوص إذا كانت خامسة؟
ar.b: تُحذف.

alfiyya.f: For a yāʾ that is the fourth radical, when is deletion preferred over changing it?
alfiyya.b: Deletion is preferable for a fourth-radical yāʾ.

ar.f: متى يفضل حذف الياء الرابعة على قلبها؟
ar.b: حذف الياء رابعةً أحقّ من قلبها.

alfiyya.f: What happens to a third-radical yāʾ in nisba formation?
alfiyya.b: It must be changed.

ar.f: ماذا يحدث للياء الثالثة في النسب؟
ar.b: يجب قلبها.

alfiyya.f: What vowel accompanies the replacement of a weak radical by wāw?
alfiyya.b: The preceding consonant is given fatḥa.

ar.f: ما حركة الحرف قبل الواو المبدلة؟
ar.b: يفتح ما قبل الواو المقلوبة.

alfiyya.f: How are the middle vowels of «فَعِل», «فُعِل», and «فِعِل» treated in nisba formation?
alfiyya.b: The first two take fatḥa on the middle radical; «فِعِل» follows the stated pattern with its specified vowel.

ar.f: كيف تضبط عين أوزان فعِل وفُعِل وفِعِل في النسب؟
ar.b: تفتح عين «فَعِل» و«فُعِل»، ويُراعى في «فِعِل» ضبطه المذكور.

alfiyya.f: What two forms are reported for nisba to «مرميّ»?
alfiyya.b: «مَرْمَوِيّ» is reported, but «مَرْمِيّ» is preferred in common usage.

ar.f: ما الوجهان في النسب إلى مرمي؟
ar.b: قيل «مَرْمَوِيّ»، والمختار في الاستعمال «مَرْمِيّ».

alfiyya.f: How is a noun like «حيّ» treated when forming nisba?
alfiyya.b: Give its second radical fatḥa; if the yāʾ was changed from wāw, restore wāw.

ar.f: كيف ينسب إلى نحو حيّ؟
ar.b: يجب فتح ثانيه، وترد الواو إن كانت الياء منقلبة عنها.

alfiyya.f: What happens to dual endings in nisba formation?
alfiyya.b: Delete the dual marker.

ar.f: ماذا يفعل بعلامة التثنية عند النسب؟
ar.b: تحذف علامة التثنية.

alfiyya.f: What happens to sound plural endings in nisba formation?
alfiyya.b: Delete the sound-plural marker as well.

ar.f: ماذا يفعل بعلامة الجمع السالم عند النسب؟
ar.b: تحذف علامة جمع التصحيح كذلك.

alfiyya.f: What happens to the third radical in forms like «طيّب» in nisba formation?
alfiyya.b: It is deleted.

ar.f: ماذا يفعل بالحرف الثالث في نحو طيب عند النسب؟
ar.b: يُحذف.

alfiyya.f: What exceptional nisba is reported for «طيّب»?
alfiyya.b: «طائيّ» is an anomalous form.

ar.f: ما النسب الشاذ إلى طيّب؟
ar.b: «طائيّ» شاذ.

alfiyya.f: What nisba pattern is required for «فَعِيلة»?
alfiyya.b: Use «فَعَليّ».

ar.f: ما وزن النسب إلى فعيلة؟
ar.b: يلزم «فَعَليّ».

alfiyya.f: What nisba pattern is required for «فُعَيْلة»?
alfiyya.b: Use «فُعَليّ».

ar.f: ما وزن النسب إلى فُعيلة؟
ar.b: يلزم «فُعَليّ».

alfiyya.f: What if a weak-final adjective does not fit either «فعيلة» pattern?
alfiyya.b: It is treated like forms ending in tāʾ.

ar.f: ماذا يفعل بالمعتل اللام إذا لم يوافق وزني فعيلة؟
ar.b: يُلحق بما ختم بالتاء.

alfiyya.f: How is a form like «الطويلة» treated in nisba formation?
alfiyya.b: Its base is completed before adding nisba, following the pattern described.

ar.f: كيف ينسب إلى نحو الطويلة؟
ar.b: يتمّ بناؤه قبل إلحاق ياء النسب.

alfiyya.f: How are extended-alif nouns treated when forming nisba?
alfiyya.b: Treat the hamza according to what occurs in the dual formation.

ar.f: كيف تعامل الأسماء الممدودة عند النسب؟
ar.b: تعامل همزتها على ما جرى في التثنية.

alfiyya.f: To which part of a sentence-name is nisba attached?
alfiyya.b: Attach it to the first component.

ar.f: إلى أي جزء ينسب في العلم المركب جملة؟
ar.b: ينسب إلى صدر الجملة.

alfiyya.f: To which part of a blend compound is nisba attached?
alfiyya.b: Attach it to the first component.

ar.f: إلى أي جزء ينسب في المركب المزجي؟
ar.b: ينسب إلى صدر المركب المزجي.

alfiyya.f: To which component is nisba attached in an annexed name beginning with «ابن» or «أب»?
alfiyya.b: It is attached to the second component.

ar.f: إلى أي جزء ينسب في الإضافة المبدوءة بابن أو أب؟
ar.b: ينسب إلى العجز.

alfiyya.f: When else is nisba attached to the second component of an annexed expression?
alfiyya.b: When definiteness is necessarily supplied by the second component.

ar.f: متى ينسب إلى عجز الإضافة أيضاً؟
ar.b: إذا كان التعريف لا يتم إلا بالثاني.

alfiyya.f: In other annexed names, which component normally receives nisba?
alfiyya.b: Normally to the first component, unless that would create ambiguity.

ar.f: في سائر الإضافات، إلى أي جزء يكون النسب؟
ar.b: ينسب إلى الأول ما لم يُخش اللبس.

alfiyya.f: How can a deleted final radical be restored in duals or sound plurals?
alfiyya.b: It may be restored to repair the form, provided the restoration does not result in an alif.

ar.f: كيف يردّ الحرف الأخير المحذوف في المثنى أو الجمع السالم؟
ar.b: يجوز جبر المحذوف برد اللام ما لم يؤدّ ردها إلى ألف.

alfiyya.f: In which forms may a deleted final radical be restored?
alfiyya.b: In the dual and the two sound plurals.

ar.f: في أي صيغ يجوز رد اللام؟
ar.b: في التثنية وجمعي التصحيح.

alfiyya.f: What is required of a restored form?
alfiyya.b: It must fully preserve the expected form.

ar.f: ما شرط الصورة المجَبورة؟
ar.b: يجب توفية حق الصورة بعد الجبر.

alfiyya.f: How may feminine counterparts be formed for kinship terms?
alfiyya.b: Add feminine «ـة», as «أخ» → «أخت».

ar.f: كيف يصاغ المؤنث من ألفاظ القرابة؟
ar.b: تلحق التاء، مثل «أخ» و«أخت».

alfiyya.f: How may a feminine counterpart of «ابن» be formed, and what disagreement is noted?
alfiyya.b: Use «بنت»; Yūnus reportedly rejected deletion of the tāʾ.

ar.f: كيف يؤنث ابن، وما الخلاف؟
ar.b: يقال «بنت»، ونُقل عن يونس إباء حذف التاء.

alfiyya.f: What is done when forming nisba from a two-letter word whose second radical is weak?
alfiyya.b: Double the second radical, as in «لا» → «لائيّ».

ar.f: ماذا يفعل في النسب إلى الثنائي الذي ثانيه حرف لين؟
ar.b: يضاعف الثاني، مثل «لا» و«لائيّ».

alfiyya.f: How is a word like «شِيَة» treated when its first radical is missing?
alfiyya.b: Restore the missing radical and give the middle vowel fatḥa.

ar.f: كيف يعامل نحو شية إذا حذفت فاؤه؟
ar.b: يُجبر المحذوف وتفتح العين.

alfiyya.f: How is nisba to a plural normally expressed?
alfiyya.b: Use the singular form as the base, unless the plural has a distinct lexical form that is not structurally like a singular.

ar.f: كيف يكون النسب إلى الجمع غالباً؟
ar.b: ينسب إلى الواحد من الجمع إلا إذا خالف الواحد في الوضع.

alfiyya.f: Which adjective patterns may express nisba without the yāʾ ending?
alfiyya.b: «فاعل», «فعّال», and «فَعِل» may serve as relational adjectives.

ar.f: ما الأوزان التي تغني عن ياء النسب؟
ar.b: قد تغني أوزان «فاعل» و«فعّال» و«فَعِل» عن ياء النسب.

alfiyya.f: How should nisba forms not covered by these rules be handled?
alfiyya.b: Follow transmitted usage and do not extend a rule without evidence.

ar.f: كيف يعامل النسب فيما لم تذكره القواعد؟
ar.b: يقتصر فيه على المنقول.

alfiyya.f: How is tanwīn pronounced at pause after fatḥa?
alfiyya.b: Change it to alif.

ar.f: كيف يوقف على التنوين بعد الفتحة؟
ar.b: يُبدل ألفاً.

alfiyya.f: How is tanwīn pronounced at pause after a vowel other than fatḥa?
alfiyya.b: Delete it.
alfiyya.s: Bayt 881 — الوقف على تنوين غير الفتح

ar.f: كيف يوقف على التنوين بعد غير الفتحة؟
ar.b: يُحذف.

alfiyya.f: What happens to a non-fatḥa vowel on a pronoun suffix at pause?
alfiyya.b: In ordinary speech, delete the lengthening vowel of the pronoun suffix, except in poetic necessity.

ar.f: ماذا يحدث لحركة صلة الضمير غير المفتوحة عند الوقف؟
ar.b: تحذف صلة الضمير غير المفتوحة في الوقف، إلا لضرورة.

alfiyya.f: How is «إذًا» stopped when it is tanwīn-like and accusative?
alfiyya.b: The nūn is changed to alif, like accusative tanwīn.

ar.f: كيف يوقف على إذن إذا نونت ونصبت؟
ar.b: تقلب نونها ألفاً في الوقف كالتنوين المنصوب.

alfiyya.f: How is the final yāʾ of a tanwīn-bearing defective noun treated at pause when it is not accusative?
alfiyya.b: Deleting its yāʾ is preferred to retaining it.

ar.f: كيف يوقف على ياء المنقوص المنون إذا لم يكن منصوباً؟
ar.b: حذف يائه أولى من إثباتها.

alfiyya.f: How is the yāʾ of a defective noun without tanwīn treated at pause?
alfiyya.b: The reverse applies: retaining the yāʾ is preferred.

ar.f: كيف يوقف على ياء المنقوص غير المنون؟
ar.b: العكس؛ إثبات الياء أولى.

alfiyya.f: What is the rule for a form like «مُرٍ» at pause?
alfiyya.b: Restore the yāʾ.

ar.f: ما حكم الوقف على نحو «مُرٍ»؟
ar.b: يجب رد الياء.

alfiyya.f: How may a final moving consonant other than feminine tāʾ be paused on?
alfiyya.b: It may be made sākin, paused with an attempted vowel (rawm), or given a hint of ḍamma (ishmām).

ar.f: كيف يوقف على الحرف المتحرك غير تاء التأنيث؟
ar.b: يسكن أو يوقف بالروم أو الإشمام.

alfiyya.f: What other pause method is described for a final consonant?
alfiyya.b: It may be doubled, provided the consonant is not hamza or weak and is preceded by a vowel.

ar.f: ما الوجه الآخر للوقف على الحرف الأخير؟
ar.b: يجوز تضعيفه إذا لم يكن همزاً أو حرف علة وكان قبله متحرك.

alfiyya.f: What is vowel transfer (naql) at pause?
alfiyya.b: A final vowel may be transferred to a preceding sākin consonant that can bear it.

ar.f: ما النقل في الوقف؟
ar.b: تنقل حركة الآخر إلى ساكن قبله يصح تحريكه.

alfiyya.f: Do Basran and Kufan grammarians agree on transferring fatḥa from a non-hamza?
alfiyya.b: No. Basrans reject it; Kufans transmit it.

ar.f: هل يتفق البصريون والكوفيون في نقل الفتحة عن غير المهموز؟
ar.b: لا؛ يمنعه البصريون وينقله الكوفيون.

alfiyya.f: When is vowel transfer not allowed?
alfiyya.b: When there is no comparable attested pattern; transfer from a hamza is an exception and is permitted.

ar.f: متى يمتنع نقل الحركة؟
ar.b: يمتنع إذا لم يوجد نظير، ويُستثنى المهموز فيجوز فيه.

alfiyya.f: How is feminine tāʾ usually pronounced at pause?
alfiyya.b: It is changed to hāʾ if it is connected in speech to a vowel rather than a sākin.

ar.f: كيف يوقف على تاء التأنيث؟
ar.b: تقلب هاءً إذا وصلت بمتحرك.

alfiyya.f: How common is this hāʾ pause in sound plurals and similar forms?
alfiyya.b: It is rare in sound plurals and similar forms.

ar.f: ما شيوع الوقف بالهاء في جمع التصحيح وما شابهه؟
ar.b: يقلّ في جمع التصحيح وما ضاهاه.

alfiyya.f: What is the usual pause treatment in other forms?
alfiyya.b: The opposite pattern applies as stated in the verse.

ar.f: ما حكم الوقف في غير جمع التصحيح وما شابهه؟
ar.b: يجري العكس في غير هذين النوعين.

alfiyya.f: When is hāʾ al-sakt used after a verb?
alfiyya.b: It may be placed at pause on a weak verb whose final radical has been deleted, such as «أعطِ».
alfiyya.s: Bayt 893 — هاء السكت مع الفعل المعتل

ar.f: متى تلحق هاء السكت بالفعل؟
ar.b: تلحق عند الوقف بالفعل المعتل المحذوف الآخر، مثل «أعطِ».

alfiyya.f: Is hāʾ al-sakt obligatory on every such weak verb?
alfiyya.b: No; it is obligatory only in forms like «عِ» or jussive «يَعِ»; elsewhere it is not required.

ar.f: هل هاء السكت واجبة في كل فعل معتل؟
ar.b: لا؛ تلزم في نحو «عِ» و«يَعِ» المجزوم، ولا تلزم في غيره.

alfiyya.f: What happens to the alif of interrogative «ما» after a preposition?
alfiyya.b: Delete the alif, and add hāʾ at pause.

ar.f: ماذا يحدث لألف ما الاستفهامية بعد حرف الجر؟
ar.b: تحذف ألفها، وتلحقها هاء الوقف.

alfiyya.f: Is hāʾ al-sakt always obligatory after preposition + interrogative «ما»?
alfiyya.b: No; it is not obligatory except in the specified case where «ما» is genitive after a noun.

ar.f: هل هاء السكت واجبة دائماً بعد ما الاستفهامية المجرورة؟
ar.b: لا تلزم إلا في الصورة التي جُرّت فيها باسم، كما في المثال.

alfiyya.f: When may hāʾ al-sakt be linked to the next word in connected speech?
alfiyya.b: It may be connected when the form is fixed-built with a required vowel.

ar.f: متى يجوز وصل هاء السكت بما بعدها؟
ar.b: يجوز وصلها بكل مبني تلزم حركته.

alfiyya.f: What is the status of connecting hāʾ al-sakt when its preceding form is not obligatorily vowelled?
alfiyya.b: It is anomalous, though it is considered more acceptable in consistently connected usage.
alfiyya.s: Bayt 898 — وصل هاء السكت بغير بناء لازم

ar.f: ما حكم وصل هاء السكت إذا لم تلزم حركة ما قبلها؟
ar.b: هو شاذ، ويُستحسن في الوصل الدائم.

alfiyya.f: Can connected pronunciation sometimes receive a pause form?
alfiyya.b: Yes; pause-like forms may occur in connected prose and are common in verse.

ar.f: هل يعطى الوصل أحياناً حكم الوقف؟
ar.b: نعم، قد يعطى الوصل لفظ الوقف في النثر، وكثر في النظم.

alfiyya.f: Which final alif is subject to imāla?
alfiyya.b: An alif at the end that has been changed from yāʾ is inclined toward yāʾ in pronunciation.
alfiyya.s: Bayt 900 — إمالة الألف المنقلبة عن ياء

ar.f: أيّ ألف متطرفة تميل؟
ar.b: تميل الألف المتطرفة المنقلبة عن ياء.

alfiyya.f: Does imāla also apply to a final alif where yāʾ replaces it?
alfiyya.b: Yes, the final alif is also inclined when yāʾ occurs in its place.

ar.f: هل تقع الإمالة في الألف التي تخلفها ياء؟
ar.b: نعم، وكذلك ما وقعت الياء خلفاً منه.

alfiyya.f: When is imāla (inclining alif toward yāʾ) allowed?
alfiyya.b: Imāla is licensed by a connected cause such as a preceding kasra or yāʾ, subject to the blocking rules that follow.

ar.f: متى تجوز الإمالة؟
ar.b: تجوز الإمالة لسبب متصل كالكسرة أو الياء، مع مراعاة الموانع الآتية.

alfiyya.f: What does the poem say about imāla when an intervening augment or irregular form is involved?
alfiyya.b: The rule is stated without an augment or irregular exception; imāla is not extended beyond the stated environments.

ar.f: ماذا يقول الناظم عن الإمالة مع وجود زائد أو شذوذ؟
ar.b: الحكم مقيد بما ورد دون زيادة أو شذوذ، فلا يتوسع فيه بلا سماع.

alfiyya.f: Which feminine-ending environment may block imāla?
alfiyya.b: A following feminine hāʾ/ending is relevant to the rule; where the intervening form lacks that hāʾ, apply the stated conditions rather than assuming a block.

ar.f: ما الموضع المتصل بتاء التأنيث الذي قد يمنع الإمالة؟
ar.b: يُراعى ما يلي هاء التأنيث؛ فإن عدمت الهاء لم يثبت هذا المانع.

alfiyya.f: When may a verb’s middle radical be treated as an imāla trigger?
alfiyya.b: When the verb’s form would yield «فِلْتُ», as in the past forms of «خِفْ» and «دِنْ».

ar.f: متى يكون بدل عين الفعل سبباً للإمالة؟
ar.b: إذا آل تصريف الفعل إلى «فِلْتُ»، كماضي «خِفْ» و«دِنْ».

alfiyya.f: Can an intervening consonant block imāla after yāʾ?
alfiyya.b: An intervening consonant may be tolerated; the hāʾ in an example like «جيبها» does not necessarily block it.
alfiyya.s: Bayt 903 — الفصل بين سبب الإمالة والألف

ar.f: هل يمنع حرف فاصل الإمالة بعد الياء؟
ar.b: يُغتفر الفصل بحرف، وكذلك مع الهاء في نحو «جيبها».

alfiyya.f: What other environments trigger imāla?
alfiyya.b: A following kasra, a kasra after the next consonant, or a sukūn preceded by kasra may trigger it.

ar.f: ما أسباب الإمالة الأخرى؟
ar.b: من أسبابها كسرة تلي الألف، أو كسرة بعد التالي، أو سكون بعد كسرة.

alfiyya.f: Does hāʾ necessarily block imāla when it separates the trigger from the alif?
alfiyya.b: No; hāʾ is treated like no separator, so imāla may remain possible, as in «درهماك».

ar.f: هل تمنع الهاء الإمالة إذا فصلت بين السبب والألف؟
ar.b: لا؛ تعد الهاء كأنها غير فاصلة، فتجوز الإمالة مثل «درهماك».

alfiyya.f: Which consonant classes can block imāla?
alfiyya.b: An emphatic/raised consonant and rāʾ may block a preceding kasra or yāʾ as a trigger.

ar.f: ما الحروف التي قد تكف الإمالة؟
ar.b: قد يكف حرف الاستعلاء والراء أثر الكسرة أو الياء.

alfiyya.f: When does a blocking emphatic or rāʾ retain its blocking force across intervening letters?
alfiyya.b: When it is directly connected, follows one letter, or is separated by two letters in the stated environments.

ar.f: متى يستمر مانع الاستعلاء أو الراء مع الفصل؟
ar.b: يكف إذا اتصل أو جاء بعد حرف أو فصل بينهما حرفان وفق القيود.

alfiyya.f: Can a preceding emphatic or rāʾ also prevent imāla?
alfiyya.b: Yes, when the preceding segment has not itself been weakened by kasra or sukūn after kasra.

ar.f: هل يمنع حرف الاستعلاء أو الراء السابق الإمالة؟
ar.b: نعم، إذا تقدم ما لم ينكسر أو يسكن بعد كسرة.

alfiyya.f: What can weaken the blocking force of an emphatic consonant or rāʾ?
alfiyya.b: Kasra on rāʾ can weaken the block, as in «غارماً لا أجفو».

ar.f: ما الذي يضعف منع الاستعلاء والراء؟
ar.b: تكف كسرة الراء مانع الاستعلاء والراء، مثل «غارماً لا أجفو».

alfiyya.f: May an unconnected trigger cause imāla?
alfiyya.b: Generally no; a cause must be connected, though a separate blocking element may still prevent imāla.

ar.f: هل تجوز الإمالة بسبب غير متصل؟
ar.b: لا تمل لسبب غير متصل، وقد يقع المنع بسبب منفصل.

alfiyya.f: Can euphonic matching alone cause imāla?
alfiyya.b: Yes, imāla may occur for phonetic harmony even without another trigger, as in the poetic examples.

ar.f: هل تكفي المناسبة الصوتية وحدها للإمالة؟
ar.b: نعم، قد تقع لمجرد التناسب الصوتي.

alfiyya.f: Which words are not normally subject to imāla without transmitted evidence?
alfiyya.b: Words lacking full morphological establishment are not inclined, except certain particles such as «ها» and «نا».

ar.f: ما الذي لا تدخله الإمالة بلا سماع؟
ar.b: لا تمل غير المتمكن إلا بسماع، ويستثنى نحو «ها» و«نا».

alfiyya.f: What vowel before final rāʾ can trigger imāla?
alfiyya.b: An alif preceded by fatḥa before a final rāʾ is inclined, as in the example «الأيسر».

ar.f: ما الحركة التي تمال معها الألف قبل الراء المتطرفة؟
ar.b: تمال الفتحة قبل الراء المتطرفة، مثل «الأيسر» في الشاهد.

alfiyya.f: When is an alif before feminine hāʾ inclined at pause?
alfiyya.b: When the preceding segment is not itself an alif consonant or its equivalent.

ar.f: متى تمال الألف قبل هاء التأنيث في الوقف؟
ar.b: تمال في الوقف إذا لم يكن ما قبل الهاء ألفاً أو ما في حكمها.

alfiyya.f: What kinds of elements are outside ordinary derivational morphology (taṣrīf)?
alfiyya.b: Particles and similar indeclinable material are not subject to ordinary derivational patterns.

ar.f: ما الذي يخرج من أبواب التصريف؟
ar.b: الحروف وما أشبهها بريئة من التصريف.

alfiyya.f: What is the minimum length of a noun that can ordinarily undergo morphological patterning?
alfiyya.b: Three radicals, except where a shorter form has been altered from a longer original.

ar.f: ما أقل عدد حروف الاسم القابل للتصريف؟
ar.b: لا يكون القابل للتصريف دون الثلاثي إلا إذا كان مغيراً عن أصل أطول.

alfiyya.f: What is the maximum length of an unaugmented noun?
alfiyya.b: An unaugmented noun may have up to five radicals.

ar.f: ما أكثر حروف الاسم المجرد؟
ar.b: غاية المجرد خمسة أحرف.

alfiyya.f: What is the maximum length of an augmented noun?
alfiyya.b: It may reach seven letters.

ar.f: ما غاية الاسم المزيد؟
ar.b: غاية المزيد سبعة أحرف.

alfiyya.f: What are the possible vowels on the first two radicals of a triliteral verb?
alfiyya.b: The first radical may take fatḥa, ḍamma, or kasra; the second may take those vowels or sukūn.

ar.f: ما حركات فاء الفعل الثلاثي وعينه؟
ar.b: تتحرك الفاء بالفتح والضم والكسر، وتتحرك العين بها أو تسكن.

alfiyya.f: Which triliteral pattern is excluded among those combinations?
alfiyya.b: «فِعُل» is not used.

ar.f: أي وزن ثلاثي مهمل؟
ar.b: أُهمل وزن «فِعُل».

alfiyya.f: Why is «فُعِل» especially associated with passive verbs?
alfiyya.b: The pattern is reserved to distinguish the passive verb form.

ar.f: لماذا خُصّ وزن فُعِل بالفعل المبني للمجهول؟
ar.b: خصّصوا «فُعِل» للفعل المبني للمجهول.

alfiyya.f: What vowels can the middle radical of a triliteral verb take?
alfiyya.b: It may take fatḥa, ḍamma, or kasra; additional forms such as «ضُمِن» also occur.

ar.f: ما حركات عين الفعل الثلاثي؟
ar.b: تفتح أو تضم أو تكسر، وترد أوزان أخرى مثل «ضُمِن».

alfiyya.f: What is the maximum length of an unaugmented verb?
alfiyya.b: An unaugmented verb may have at most four radicals.

ar.f: ما غاية الفعل المجرد؟
ar.b: غاية المجرد أربعة أحرف.

alfiyya.f: What is the maximum length of an augmented verb?
alfiyya.b: It may reach six letters.

ar.f: ما غاية الفعل المزيد؟
ar.b: غاية المزيد ستة أحرف.

alfiyya.f: What patterns are listed for unaugmented quadriliteral nouns?
alfiyya.b: «فَعْلَل، فِعْلِل، فِعْلَل، فُعْلُل», with «فِعَلّ» also listed.

ar.f: ما أوزان الرباعي المجرد المذكورة؟
ar.b: أوزانه «فَعْلَل، فِعْلِل، فِعْلَل، فُعْلُل»، ومعها «فِعَلّ».

alfiyya.f: What additional pattern is included for unaugmented quadriliteral nouns?
alfiyya.b: «فُعْلَل».

ar.f: ما الوزن الآخر للرباعي المجرد؟
ar.b: «فُعْلَل».

alfiyya.f: What patterns are listed for nouns longer than four letters?
alfiyya.b: The poem lists «فَعَلَّل، فَعْلَلِل، فُعَلِّل، فِعْلَلّ» and related forms.

ar.f: ما أوزان الاسم الزائد على أربعة أحرف؟
ar.b: يذكر «فَعَلَّل، فَعْلَلِل، فُعَلِّل، فِعْلَلّ» وما شابهها.

alfiyya.f: How are letters distinguished as radicals or augments when constructing a morphological pattern?
alfiyya.b: A letter that is fixed in the root is radical; a nonfixed added letter is an augment, like the tāʾ of «احتذى».

ar.f: كيف يميز الأصل من الزائد في الميزان؟
ar.b: اللازم أصل، وغير اللازم زائد، مثل تاء «احتذى».

alfiyya.f: How is an original letter represented in the morphological scale?
alfiyya.b: Use the corresponding root slot «ف، ع، ل» and repeat «ل» for additional radicals.

ar.f: كيف يرمز إلى الحرف الأصلي في الميزان؟
ar.b: يقابل الأصل بفاء الميزان أو عينه أو لامه، وتكرر اللام للزائد من الأصول.

alfiyya.f: How are augment letters represented in the scale?
alfiyya.b: Represent an augment by its own written letter in the scale.

ar.f: كيف تمثل حروف الزيادة في الميزان؟
ar.b: يثبت الزائد بلفظه في الميزان.

alfiyya.f: How is a repeated root consonant represented in the scale?
alfiyya.b: Repeat the corresponding root slot, as the rāʾ in «جعفر» or qāf in «فستق».

ar.f: كيف يوزن الحرف الأصلي المكرر؟
ar.b: يكرر حرف الميزان المقابل للأصل، مثل راء جعفر وقاف فستق.

alfiyya.f: If an augment duplicates a root letter, how is it represented?
alfiyya.b: Give the augment the same symbol as the radical it duplicates.

ar.f: إذا كان الزائد من جنس حرف أصلي، كيف يوزن؟
ar.b: يعطى الزائد وزن الأصل الذي ضوعف منه.

alfiyya.f: How are the letters in «سمسم» treated when assigning the pattern?
alfiyya.b: They are treated as original radicals.

ar.f: كيف تعامل حروف «سمسم» في الميزان؟
ar.b: يُحكم بأصالة حروفه.

alfiyya.f: Is the root analysis of forms like «لملم» agreed upon?
alfiyya.b: No; grammarians differ.

ar.f: هل يتفق في أصول نحو «لملم»؟
ar.b: فيه خلاف.

alfiyya.f: When is an alif usually an augment?
alfiyya.b: When it accompanies more than two established radicals.

ar.f: متى تكون الألف زائدة غالباً؟
ar.b: إذا صحبت أكثر من حرفين أصليين.

alfiyya.f: When are yāʾ and wāw usually treated as augments?
alfiyya.b: When they do not occur as radicals in the root, unlike repeated-root examples such as «يؤيؤ» and «وعوع».

ar.f: متى تكون الياء والواو زائدتين؟
ar.b: إذا لم تقعا أصلين، بخلاف نحو «يؤيؤ» و«وعوع».

alfiyya.f: When are initial hamza and mīm considered augments?
alfiyya.b: When three root radicals are already established after them.

ar.f: متى تحكم بزيادة الهمزة والميم في الأول؟
ar.b: إذا تحقق بعدهما ثلاثة أصول.

alfiyya.f: When is a final hamza considered an augment?
alfiyya.b: When it follows an alif after more than two root letters.

ar.f: متى تكون الهمزة المتطرفة زائدة؟
ar.b: إذا وقعت بعد ألف وتقدّمها أكثر من حرفين أصليين.

alfiyya.f: When is final nūn treated like final hamza as an augment?
alfiyya.b: In analogous positions; but nūn is original in forms such as «غضنفر».

ar.f: متى تكون النون المتطرفة كالهمزة في الزيادة؟
ar.b: في موضعها النظير، لكنها أصلية في نحو «غضنفر».

alfiyya.f: When is tāʾ an augment?
alfiyya.b: In feminine marking, present-tense formation, patterns like «استفعال», and verb forms expressing reflexive/causative response.

ar.f: متى تكون التاء زائدة؟
ar.b: تكون زائدة للتأنيث والمضارعة وفي نحو الاستفعال والمطاوعة.

alfiyya.f: When is hāʾ an augment?
alfiyya.b: As a pause marker, as in «لِمَهْ» or «لم تره».

ar.f: متى تكون الهاء زائدة؟
ar.b: تكون زائدة للوقف، مثل «لمه» و«لم تره».

alfiyya.f: When is lām an augment?
alfiyya.b: In the familiar demonstrative forms.

ar.f: متى تكون اللام زائدة؟
ar.b: في لام أسماء الإشارة المشهورة.

alfiyya.f: Can an augment be asserted without evidence?
alfiyya.b: No; do not posit an augment unless a clear argument supports it.

ar.f: هل يحكم بزيادة حرف بلا دليل؟
ar.b: لا تثبت زيادة بلا قيد أو حجة واضحة.

alfiyya.f: When is hamzat al-waṣl pronounced?
alfiyya.b: It is pronounced only when beginning speech; it disappears in connected speech.

ar.f: متى تنطق همزة الوصل؟
ar.b: لا تثبت إلا في الابتداء وتسقط في الوصل.

alfiyya.f: In which past-tense verbs does hamzat al-waṣl occur?
alfiyya.b: In past verbs with more than four letters, such as «انجلى».

ar.f: في أي ماضٍ تأتي همزة الوصل؟
ar.b: في الماضي الزائد على أربعة أحرف، مثل «انجلى».

alfiyya.f: Where else does hamzat al-waṣl occur in those verb patterns?
alfiyya.b: In their imperative and verbal noun.
alfiyya.s: Bayt 940 — همزة الوصل في الأمر والمصدر

ar.f: أين تأتي همزة الوصل أيضاً في هذه الأوزان؟
ar.b: في أمرها ومصدرها.

alfiyya.f: Does the triliteral imperative take hamzat al-waṣl?
alfiyya.b: Yes, as in «اخشَ، امضِ، انفذ».

ar.f: هل تأتي همزة الوصل في أمر الثلاثي؟
ar.b: نعم، مثل «اخشَ» و«امضِ» و«انفذ».

alfiyya.f: Which lexical nouns are listed with hamzat al-waṣl?
alfiyya.b: «اسم، است، ابن، ابنم، اثنان، امرؤ», plus feminine forms derived from them.

ar.f: ما الأسماء السماعية التي تذكر لهمزة الوصل؟
ar.b: «اسم، است، ابن، ابنم، اثنان، امرؤ» وما ألحق بتأنيثها.

alfiyya.f: What special oath word is listed with hamzat al-waṣl?
alfiyya.b: «اَيْمُن» in oath expressions.

ar.f: ما لفظ القسم المذكور بهمزة الوصل؟
ar.b: «اَيْمُن» في القسم.

alfiyya.f: What is the hamza in the definite article?
alfiyya.b: It is hamzat al-waṣl.

ar.f: ما حكم همزة أل التعريف؟
ar.b: همزة «أل» همزة وصل.

alfiyya.f: How is hamza treated in an interrogative before a word beginning with hamza?
alfiyya.b: It may be changed to a long vowel or eased in pronunciation.

ar.f: كيف تعامل الهمزة في الاستفهام إذا اجتمعت مع همزة أخرى؟
ar.b: قد تبدل مداً أو تسهّل.

alfiyya.f: What mnemonic lists the consonants that may replace hamza?
alfiyya.b: «هَدَأْتَ مُوطِيَا» lists hāʾ, dāl, hamza, tāʾ, mīm, wāw, ṭāʾ, yāʾ, and alif-related categories as stated.

ar.f: ما أحرف الإبدال التي جمعها الناظم؟
ar.b: جمعت في «هَدَأْتَ مُوطِيَا» أحرف الإبدال المذكورة.

alfiyya.f: When is hamza replaced by wāw or yāʾ at the end of a word?
alfiyya.b: When it is final after an added alif, and in the relevant hollow active participle.

ar.f: متى تبدل الهمزة واواً أو ياءً في الطرف؟
ar.b: تبدل في الطرف بعد ألف زائدة، وفي فاعل الأجوف المعتل عينه.

alfiyya.f: Why does a long vowel in third position sometimes become hamza in a singular?
alfiyya.b: The pattern may require hamza, as seen in the singular counterpart of «قلائد».

ar.f: لماذا تقلب مدة المفرد الثالثة همزة أحياناً؟
ar.b: تقلب همزة إذا اقتضى الوزن، مثل مفرد «قلائد».

alfiyya.f: When does the second of two weak letters become hamza in a plural?
alfiyya.b: When two weak letters frame the long vowel of a «مفاعل» plural pattern.

ar.f: متى تهمز الثانية من لينين في الجمع؟
ar.b: إذا اكتنف حرفا لين مدّ مفاعل، كما في الجمع المذكور.

alfiyya.f: When a final weak radical becomes hamza, what happens to its vowel?
alfiyya.b: Give it fatḥa.

ar.f: إذا أبدلت اللام المعتلة همزة، ما حركتها؟
ar.b: تفتح.

alfiyya.f: When may a final weak radical be restored as yāʾ?
alfiyya.b: In a form whose final radical was weakened, restore yāʾ where the underlying form requires it.

ar.f: متى ترد اللام المعتلة ياء؟
ar.b: ترد ياءً في المعتل اللام بحسب الأصل.

alfiyya.f: How is the first of two initial wāws treated in some words?
alfiyya.b: It may be replaced by hamza, except in forms resembling «وُوفي» under the stated exception.

ar.f: كيف تعامل الواو الأولى من واوين في أول الكلمة؟
ar.b: قد تبدل الهمزة من الأولى إلا في نحو «وُوفي» وما استثني.

alfiyya.f: What happens to the second of two hamzas in one word when it is sākin?
alfiyya.b: It is replaced by a long vowel, as in «آثر» and «ائتمن».

ar.f: ماذا يحدث للهمزة الثانية الساكنة في كلمة؟
ar.b: تبدل حرف مد، مثل «آثر» و«ائتمن».

alfiyya.f: How does the vowel before a second hamza affect its replacement?
alfiyya.b: After ḍamma or fatḥa it becomes wāw; after kasra it becomes yāʾ.

ar.f: كيف تؤثر حركة ما قبل الهمزة الثانية في الإبدال؟
ar.b: تقلب واواً بعد الضم والفتح، وياءً بعد الكسر.

alfiyya.f: What if the second hamza itself is vowelled with kasra?
alfiyya.b: It is replaced by yāʾ in all cases.

ar.f: ماذا إذا كانت الهمزة الثانية مكسورة؟
ar.b: تقلب ياءً مطلقاً.

alfiyya.f: What if the second hamza is vowelled with ḍamma?
alfiyya.b: It normally becomes wāw, unless the word form is fully fixed and requires another treatment.

ar.f: ماذا إذا كانت الهمزة الثانية مضمومة؟
ar.b: تقلب واواً ما لم تكن الكلمة تامة اللفظ لها حكم خاص.

alfiyya.f: What happens in fixed forms such as «أؤمّ»?
alfiyya.b: The second hamza may be yāʾ in any vowel context; forms like «أؤمّ» allow two treatments of the second hamza.

ar.f: ما الوجه في لفظ ثابت مثل «أؤمّ»؟
ar.b: قد تأتي ياءً مطلقاً، وفي نحو «أؤمّ» وجهان في الهمزة الثانية.

alfiyya.f: When can yāʾ be changed to alif?
alfiyya.b: When preceded by kasra in the specified word-final environments or before feminine tāʾ.

ar.f: متى تقلب الياء ألفاً؟
ar.b: تقلب الياء ألفاً بعد كسرة في الطرف أو قبل تاء التأنيث في المواضع المذكورة.

alfiyya.f: What other endings allow that yāʾ-to-alif change?
alfiyya.b: Before the endings of «فَعْلان» and related augmentations.

ar.f: ما الزيادات الأخرى التي يقع قبلها قلب الياء ألفاً؟
ar.b: يقع كذلك قبل زيادتي «فعلان» وما ألحق به.

alfiyya.f: What happens to yāʾ in a hollow weak verb’s verbal noun?
alfiyya.b: Yāʾ may become alif in the verbal noun; the corresponding «فِعَل» form is often sound, as in «الحِوَل».

ar.f: ماذا يحدث للياء في مصدر الفعل الأجوف؟
ar.b: قد تقلب ألفاً في المصدر، ويصح نظيره على «فِعَل» غالباً مثل «الحِوَل».

alfiyya.f: How are plurals formed from nouns with a weak or silent middle radical treated?
alfiyya.b: Apply the same weakening rule to the plural wherever its conditions occur.

ar.f: كيف يعامل جمع الاسم المعتل العين أو الساكنها؟
ar.b: يجري فيه الإعلال نفسه متى تحققت علته.

alfiyya.f: Is the «فِعَلة» plural of such nouns weakened?
alfiyya.b: It is generally kept sound.

ar.f: هل يعلّ جمع فِعَلة؟
ar.b: يصحح «فِعَلة».

alfiyya.f: What are the two possibilities for the «فِعَل» plural?
alfiyya.b: Both soundness and weakening occur; weakening is preferred, as in «الحِيَل».

ar.f: ما الوجهان في جمع فِعَل؟
ar.b: فيه وجهان، والإعلال أولى، مثل «الحِيَل».

alfiyya.f: What happens to wāw as a final radical after fatḥa?
alfiyya.b: It changes to yāʾ, as in the dual-like examples in the verse.

ar.f: ماذا يحدث للواو لاماً بعد فتحة؟
ar.b: تقلب الواو ياءً بعد الفتح.

alfiyya.f: What happens to wāw after ḍamma in the stated environment?
alfiyya.b: A wāw following ḍamma may be replaced by alif according to the rule.

ar.f: ماذا يحدث للواو بعد الضمة في الموضع المذكور؟
ar.b: تبدل الواو بعد الضمة ألفاً وفق الحكم.

alfiyya.f: What does the example «موقن» illustrate?
alfiyya.b: It illustrates the relevant replacement/weakening of a yāʾ in the stated environment.

ar.f: ماذا يوضح مثال «موقن»؟
ar.b: يوضح إعلال الياء في البيئة المذكورة.

alfiyya.f: What vowel change may occur in the plural of an adjective like «أهيَم»?
alfiyya.b: The originally ḍamma-vowelled weak radical is given kasra, as in «هِيم».

ar.f: ما التغيير في جمع وصف مثل أهيم؟
ar.b: تكسر حركة المعتل المضموم في الجمع، مثل «هِيم».

alfiyya.f: When is yāʾ restored as wāw after ḍamma?
alfiyya.b: When it is the final radical of a verb or occurs before feminine tāʾ in the relevant pattern.

ar.f: متى ترد الياء واواً بعد ضمة؟
ar.b: ترد إذا كانت لام فعل أو وقعت قبل تاء التأنيث في الموضع المذكور.

alfiyya.f: What further environments are given for restoring yāʾ to wāw?
alfiyya.b: In forms such as the tāʾ derivative of «رمى» and the cited pattern «مقدرة».

ar.f: ما المواضع الأخرى لرد الياء واواً؟
ar.b: في نحو تاء «رمى» ومثل «مقدرة».

alfiyya.f: How is the weak middle radical of an adjective on «فُعْلى» treated?
alfiyya.b: Both alternatives are reported.

ar.f: كيف تعامل عين الوصف على وزن فعلى؟
ar.b: ورد فيه الوجهان.

alfiyya.f: What is the usual substitution at the end of a noun on «فَعْلى»?
alfiyya.b: Wāw commonly replaces yāʾ, as in «تقوى».

ar.f: ما القلب الغالب في لام الاسم على فعلى؟
ar.b: تقلب الياء واواً غالباً، مثل «تقوى».

alfiyya.f: What is the usual substitution at the end of an adjective on «فُعْلى»?
alfiyya.b: The reverse change occurs; «قصوى» is a rare exception.

ar.f: ما القلب الغالب في لام الوصف على فعلى؟
ar.b: يأتي العكس في الوصف، و«قصوى» نادرة.

alfiyya.f: When do adjacent wāw and yāʾ undergo assimilation?
alfiyya.b: When they are adjacent, the first is sākin, and they are not separated by an intervening/contingent element.

ar.f: متى تدغم الواو والياء المتجاورتان؟
ar.b: إذا اجتمعتا وكان السابق ساكناً وخليتا من الفصل العارض.

alfiyya.f: What is the result when wāw precedes yāʾ under those conditions?
alfiyya.b: Change the wāw to yāʾ and assimilate the two.

ar.f: ماذا يحدث إذا تقدمت الواو على الياء؟
ar.b: تقلب الواو ياءً ثم تدغم.

alfiyya.f: Are all similar forms regular?
alfiyya.b: No; the verse notes anomalous exceptions to the stated pattern.

ar.f: هل كل ما شابه ذلك قياسي؟
ar.b: لا؛ وردت شواذ تخالف القاعدة.

alfiyya.f: When is an original moving wāw or yāʾ changed to alif?
alfiyya.b: When it follows fatḥa directly and the next radical is vowelled.

ar.f: متى تقلب الواو أو الياء المتحركة ألفاً؟
ar.b: إذا وقعت بعد فتحة متصلة وكان التالي متحركاً.

alfiyya.f: What blocks this weakening when the following radical is sākin?
alfiyya.b: Sukūn blocks weakening of a non-final radical.

ar.f: ما الذي يمنع الإعلال إذا سكن الحرف التالي؟
ar.b: يمنع السكون إعلال غير اللام.

alfiyya.f: Does sukūn block weakening of a final radical?
alfiyya.b: No; final radicals are not blocked in the same way.

ar.f: هل يمنع السكون إعلال اللام؟
ar.b: لا يمنع إعلال اللام.

alfiyya.f: Which following consonant may still allow weakening of a final weak radical?
alfiyya.b: A non-alif sākin, or a yāʾ marked by gemination, may allow it.

ar.f: أيّ ساكن لا يمنع إعلال اللام؟
ar.b: قد لا يمنعه ساكن غير الألف أو ياء التشديد.

alfiyya.f: Which «أفعل» adjectives retain a sound middle radical?
alfiyya.b: Some adjectives such as «أغيد» and «أحول» retain a sound middle radical.

ar.f: أيّ أوصاف أفعل تصح فيها العين؟
ar.b: تصح عين نحو «أغيد» و«أحول».

alfiyya.f: When is the wāw of an «افتعل»-type verb retained in a related «تفاعل» form?
alfiyya.b: When the related form is built as «تفاعل», the middle radical is wāw, and no weakening has occurred.

ar.f: متى تصح واو افتعل في صيغة تفاعل؟
ar.b: إذا بني «تفاعل» من افتعل وكانت عينه واواً سلمت ولم تعلّ.

alfiyya.f: If two radicals qualify for weakening, which one normally remains sound?
alfiyya.b: Normally the first is kept sound; sometimes the reverse occurs.

ar.f: إذا استحق حرفان الإعلال، فأيهما يصحح؟
ar.b: يصحح الأول غالباً، وقد يقع العكس.

alfiyya.f: What happens to the middle radical of a noun with a noun-specific ending?
alfiyya.b: It must remain sound.

ar.f: ماذا يحدث لعين الاسم الذي لحقته زيادة مختصة بالاسم؟
ar.b: يجب أن تسلم عينه.

alfiyya.f: What happens to nūn sākin before bāʾ?
alfiyya.b: It changes to mīm, as in connected pronunciation «مَنْ بَتَّ».

ar.f: ماذا يحدث للنون الساكنة قبل الباء؟
ar.b: تقلب ميماً، مثل «من بتّ» في الوصل.

alfiyya.f: When may a weak middle radical transfer its vowel to a preceding sākin?
alfiyya.b: When the weak radical is the middle of a verb and the preceding consonant can receive the vowel.

ar.f: متى تنقل حركة حرف العلة إلى الساكن قبله؟
ar.b: تنقل إذا كان حرف اللين عين فعل وصحّ نقل حركته إلى الساكن قبله.

alfiyya.f: Which verbs are excluded from this vowel transfer?
alfiyya.b: Verbs of exclamation, doubled forms like «ابيضّ», and forms with a weak final radical such as «أهوى».

ar.f: ما الأفعال المستثناة من نقل الحركة؟
ar.b: يستثنى فعل التعجب والمضعف كـ«ابيضّ» والمعتل اللام كـ«أهوى».

alfiyya.f: Can a noun undergo the same vowel transfer as a verb?
alfiyya.b: Yes, if the noun resembles a present-tense verb and has the relevant morphological sign.

ar.f: هل يجري النقل في الاسم؟
ar.b: نعم، إذا شابه المضارع ووجدت فيه علامته.

alfiyya.f: Which derived noun patterns commonly retain a sound form instead of weakening?
alfiyya.b: «مِفْعَل», «مِفْعال», and forms with the alif of «إفعال» or «استفعال» are kept sound in the cited rule.

ar.f: ما الأبنية التي تصحح غالباً؟
ar.b: يصحح «مِفعل» و«مفعال» وألفا «إفعال» و«استفعال» وفق هذا الباب.

alfiyya.f: What happens to the alif in verbal nouns «إفعال» and «استفعال» under the weakening rule?
alfiyya.b: It is deleted for the stated weakening, and tāʾ is used as compensation.

ar.f: ماذا يحدث لألف إفعال واستفعال؟
ar.b: تحذف الألف للإعلال، وتلزم التاء عوضاً.

alfiyya.f: Can the compensatory tāʾ ever be absent?
alfiyya.b: Yes, deletion is occasionally transmitted.

ar.f: هل تحذف تاء التعويض؟
ar.b: قد تحذف بالنقل أحياناً.

alfiyya.f: Do the deletion and vowel-transfer rules also apply to the passive participle?
alfiyya.b: Yes, a passive participle may undergo the same changes.

ar.f: هل يجري الحذف والنقل في اسم المفعول؟
ar.b: يجري في اسم المفعول ما جرى في إفعال من الحذف والنقل.

alfiyya.f: Give examples of passive participles affected by these rules.
alfiyya.b: «مبيع» and «مصون».

ar.f: اذكر مثالين لاسم المفعول المتأثر بهذه القواعد.
ar.b: «مبيع» و«مصون».

alfiyya.f: How common is sound formation of a wāw-root passive participle?
alfiyya.b: It is rare.

ar.f: ما شيوع التصحيح في اسم المفعول الواوي؟
ar.b: تصحيح ذي الواو نادر.

alfiyya.f: How common is the weakened form of a yāʾ-root passive participle?
alfiyya.b: It is common.

ar.f: ما شيوع الإعلال في اسم المفعول اليائي؟
ar.b: الإعلال في ذي الياء مشهور.

alfiyya.f: How is the passive participle of a verb like «عدا» treated?
alfiyya.b: Keep it sound in the preferred form.

ar.f: كيف يصاغ اسم المفعول من نحو عدا؟
ar.b: يصحح اسم المفعول من نحو «عدا».

alfiyya.f: When may that passive participle be weakened instead?
alfiyya.b: If the better sound form is not pursued, weakening is also used.

ar.f: متى يعلّ اسم المفعول من عدا؟
ar.b: يعلّ إذا لم يتحرّ الأجود.

alfiyya.f: What two forms may occur in «فُعول» from a wāw-final root?
alfiyya.b: Both soundness and weakening are reported, whether the form is singular or plural.

ar.f: ما الوجهان في فعول من ذي الواو؟
ar.b: يرد فيه التصحيح والإعلال في المفرد والجمع.

alfiyya.f: Which plural pronunciation is common for «نُوَّم»?
alfiyya.b: «نُيَّم» is common.

ar.f: ما الجمع الشائع لنُوّام؟
ar.b: يشاع «نُيَّم».

alfiyya.f: What is the status of «نُيَّام»?
alfiyya.b: It is reported as anomalous.

ar.f: ما حكم نُيّام؟
ar.b: نُيّام شاذ.

alfiyya.f: What substitution occurs in «افتعال» when its first radical is weak?
alfiyya.b: The weak initial radical is changed to tāʾ.

ar.f: ما الإبدال في افتعال إذا كانت فاؤه حرف لين؟
ar.b: تبدل فاء افتعال اللينة تاءً.

alfiyya.f: Is the same substitution regular with an initial hamza?
alfiyya.b: No; examples like «ائتكل» are anomalous.

ar.f: هل يجري ذلك مع الهمزة؟
ar.b: لا؛ هو شاذ في نحو «ائتكل».

alfiyya.f: What happens to tāʾ of «افتعال» after an emphatic consonant?
alfiyya.b: It changes to ṭāʾ, as in the cited assimilated forms.

ar.f: ماذا يحدث لتاء افتعال بعد حرف مطبق؟
ar.b: تبدل طاءً بعد المطبق.

alfiyya.f: What happens to tāʾ of «افتعال» after a dental consonant such as dāl?
alfiyya.b: It assimilates to the preceding consonant, producing a doubled consonant, as in «ادّان» and «ادّكر».

ar.f: ماذا يحدث لتاء افتعال بعد الدال؟
ar.b: تدغم في الدال ونحوها، مثل «ادّان» و«ادّكر».

alfiyya.f: What happens to the first wāw of a verb like «وَعَد» in the imperative and present?
alfiyya.b: It is deleted in the imperative and present forms.

ar.f: ماذا يحدث لفاء الفعل الواوي مثل وعد في الأمر والمضارع؟
ar.b: تحذف في الأمر والمضارع.

alfiyya.f: Does that deletion extend to the verbal noun «عِدة»?
alfiyya.b: Yes, it is regular in the cited verbal noun.

ar.f: هل يمتد حذف الواو إلى مصدر مثل عدة؟
ar.b: نعم، يطرد في نحو «عِدة».

alfiyya.f: When is the hamza of «أفعل» deleted?
alfiyya.b: It is regularly deleted in the present-tense form and in the two derived formations specified by the poem.

ar.f: متى تحذف همزة أفعل؟
ar.b: تحذف في المضارع والبنيتين المشتقتين المذكورتين.

alfiyya.f: What contracted forms are reported from «ظَلِلْتُ»?
alfiyya.b: «ظَلْتُ» and «ظِلْتُ».

ar.f: ما الصيغتان المخففتان من ظللت؟

alfiyya.f: What contracted imperative forms are reported from «اقرِرْنَ»?
alfiyya.b: «قِرْنَ» and «قَرْنَ».

ar.f: ما الصيغتان المنقولتان من اقررن؟

alfiyya.f: What is the general rule for two consecutive moving identical consonants in one word?
alfiyya.b: They are generally assimilated into one doubled consonant.

ar.f: ما حكم المثلين المتحركين المتواليين في كلمة؟
ar.b: يدغم أولهما في الثاني غالباً.

alfiyya.f: Which forms resist that assimilation?
alfiyya.b: Some patterns such as «صُفَف، ذُلُل، كِلَل، لَبَب» retain separation.

ar.f: ما الألفاظ التي لا يدغم فيها المثلان؟
ar.b: تبقى مفكوكة في أوزان وألفاظ مثل «صُفَف» و«ذُلُل» و«كِلَل» و«لَبَب».

alfiyya.f: Do two identical consonants assimilate in forms like «جُسَّس»?
alfiyya.b: No; this and comparable forms are excluded.

ar.f: هل يدغم المثلان في نحو جسس؟
ar.b: لا؛ يستثنى نحو «جُسَّس» وما ماثله.

alfiyya.f: Do two identical consonants assimilate in «اخصص أبي»?
alfiyya.b: The poem excludes this form from ordinary assimilation.

ar.f: هل يدغم المثلان في اخصص أبي؟
ar.b: يستثنى «اخصص أبي» من الحكم العام.

alfiyya.f: Does «هيلل» follow the general assimilation rule?
alfiyya.b: No, it is an exception.

ar.f: هل يدغم في هيلل؟
ar.b: لا؛ هو من المستثنى.

alfiyya.f: Can an anomalous form like «أَلِلْ» retain separated identical letters?
alfiyya.b: Yes; such separation is accepted when supported by transmitted usage.

ar.f: هل يجوز فك الإدغام في شاذ مثل ألِل؟
ar.b: نعم، يقبل الفك في الشاذ المنقول.

alfiyya.f: What are the two possible treatments of «حيي»?
alfiyya.b: It may remain separated or be assimilated.

ar.f: ما الوجهان في حيِي؟
ar.b: يجوز فكه وإدغامه.

alfiyya.f: What other forms allow both separation and assimilation?
alfiyya.b: Forms such as «تتجلّى» and «استتر».

ar.f: ما الأفعال الأخرى التي يجوز فيها الوجهان؟
ar.b: نحو «تتجلّى» و«استتر».

alfiyya.f: Can a verb beginning with two tāʾs be shortened?
alfiyya.b: Yes, it may be reduced to one tāʾ, as in the cited form «تبيّن».

ar.f: هل يجوز اختصار الفعل المبدوء بتاءين؟
ar.b: قد يقتصر على تاء واحدة، مثل «تبيّن».

alfiyya.f: When must identical consonants be separated rather than assimilated?
alfiyya.b: When the assimilated consonant is followed by a pronoun that marks the subject, the consonants are separated.
alfiyya.s: Bayt 996 — فك الإدغام مع ضمير الرفع

ar.f: متى يجب فك الإدغام؟
ar.b: يفك إذا اتصل به ضمير رفع، مثل «حللتُ».

alfiyya.f: What example illustrates separation before a subject pronoun?
alfiyya.b: «حللتُ ما حللتَه».

ar.f: ما مثال فك الإدغام مع ضمير الرفع؟
ar.b: «حللتُ ما حللتَه».

alfiyya.f: What options are available in jussive or jussive-like forms?
alfiyya.b: Both separation and assimilation may be used.

ar.f: ما الوجهان في الجزم وشبهه؟
ar.b: يجوز الفك والإدغام.

alfiyya.f: What is required in the imperative of «أفعل» used for exclamation?
alfiyya.b: Separation is required.

ar.f: ما حكم فك الإدغام في أمر أفعل التعجبي؟
ar.b: يجب الفك.

alfiyya.f: What is the required form of «هلمّ»?
alfiyya.b: Assimilation is required.

ar.f: ما حكم الإدغام في هلم؟
ar.b: يجب الإدغام.

alfiyya.f: What does the poet claim about the Alfiyyah’s subject matter at Bayt 999?
alfiyya.b: He says he has completed the intended compilation, covering most of the important topics.

ar.f: ماذا يقرر الناظم عن موضوعات الألفية في البيت 999؟
ar.b: يعلن إتمام النظم الذي قصده واشتماله على جلّ المهمات.

alfiyya.f: What earlier work does the poet say the Khulāṣa summarizes?
alfiyya.b: It summarizes the «Kāfiya».

ar.f: ما الكتاب الذي يقول الناظم إن الخلاصة أحصته؟
ar.b: الخلاصة تحصي مسائل «الكافية».

alfiyya.f: What does the title «الخلاصة» suggest in the closing verse?
alfiyya.b: It is a concise summary intended to provide sufficiency without narrow restriction.

ar.f: ماذا يفيد اسم «الخلاصة» في البيت الختامي؟
ar.b: هي خلاصة تقصد الغنى والكفاية من غير اختصاص ضيق.

alfiyya.f: Whom does Ibn Mālik praise and invoke blessings upon in the closing lines?
alfiyya.b: He praises God and invokes blessings on Muḥammad, the best of the messengers.

ar.f: على من يصلي ابن مالك في ختام الألفية؟
ar.b: يحمد الله ويصلي على محمد خير النبيين المرسلين.

alfiyya.f: Who else is included in the closing prayer?
alfiyya.b: The Prophet’s ﷺ noble, righteous family and his chosen, excellent Companions.

ar.f: من يشملهم الدعاء في ختام النظم؟
ar.b: آله الكرام البررة وصحبه المنتخبون الأخيار.

proofs.f: What are the literal and technical definitions of taqlid?
proofs.b:
• Literal definition: The verbal noun derived from the Arabic root q-l-d, which means to place, gird, or adorn with a necklace. 

• Technical definition: The acceptance of another's statement without demanding proof or evidence, on the belief that the statement is being made in accordance with fact and proof.

proofs.f: How is taqlid present and necessary in everyday life, language, learning, and society?
proofs.b:
• Language & Learning: If we had refused to accept unquestionably (without demanding proof) the commands and teachings of our parents and teachers, we would not have learned our mother tongue, the alphabet, or the study and writing of books. 

• Specialized Knowledge: Proficiency in any branch of knowledge requires accepting its technical terminology and linguistic usages through taqlid (without questioning the authority of the terminology). 

• Social & Practical Life: Human life—eating, drinking, walking, earning—and societal progress (such as an army following a commander's orders or governments enforcing laws) are firmly rooted in taqlid (accepting and obeying professional authority).

proofs.f: What are the two types of wujub (compulsory nature) in jurisprudence (wujub bi 'l-dhat and wujub bi 'l-ghayr), and how do they apply to the preservation of the Qur'an and Hadith versus taqlid?
proofs.b:
• Wujub bi 'l-dhat ("compulsory in itself"): Acts ordered or prohibited by Islamic law due to their intrinsic nature, like the command of prayer and the prohibition of polytheism. 

• Wujub bi 'l-ghayr ("compulsory due to an external factor"): Acts that are not compulsory in themselves, but constitute the basis for other actions that are specifically commanded or prohibited in the Qur'an and hadiths. 

• Application: Preserving the Qur'an and hadith is categorically commanded (wujub bi 'l-dhat). Because such preservation is not normally possible without recording them in writing, writing them down has been decreed as wajib (wujub bi 'l-ghayr) based on necessity and the consensus of the Umma. In the exact same way, taqlid ("following someone in matters of Islamic law") is also decreed as essential or wajib.

proofs.f: How does the hadith of Aswad ibn Yazid (Sahih al-Bukhari 2:297) regarding Mu'adh ibn Jabal رضي الله عنه ؓ in Yemen serve as evidence for the validity and practice of taqlid and taqlid shakhsi during the time of the Prophet ﷺ?
proofs.b:
• Example of Taqlid: When Mu'adh رضي الله عنه decreed half the estate for a daughter and half for a sister, the questioner accepted the ruling without demanding proof or a basis, relying on Mu'adh's رضي الله عنه integrity, piety, and righteousness. 

• Approval by the Messenger ﷺ: The Prophet ﷺ did not criticize the people for following Mu'adh رضي الله عنه, nor did he raise any objections. 

• Proof for Taqlid Shakhsi: The Prophet ﷺ appointed Mu'adh رضي الله عنه to provide religious instruction to the people of Yemen, granting them the right and permission to refer to Mu'adh رضي الله عنه in all affairs of the Din, demonstrating that following a particular person in Islamic law was prevalent during the time of the Messenger ﷺ.

proofs.f: What are some of the stated negative consequences and evils of discarding taqlid?
proofs.b:
• People do not model their lives after the example of the Prophet ﷺ, leading to selfishness, corrupt motives, lust, anarchy, and opposition to consensus. 

• The absence of taqlid shakhsi leads to the rise of self-appointed mujtahids who consider themselves capable of inferring rulings through analogical reasoning (qiyas), claiming equal or greater rank than early mujtahids. 

• It opens the door to modernist claims—such as arguing that wudu' for prayer was merely for early Arabs exposed to impurities and is no longer necessary under modern hygiene—undermining clear rulings of the Shari'a.

proofs.f: How does Mufti Taqi 'Uthmani respond to the objection that following an Imam in matters of Shari'a is shirk (polytheism) or a reprehensible innovation (bid'a)?
proofs.b:
• True Obedience: True obedience belongs to Allah alone. Obedience to the Messenger ﷺ is ordered because he conveyed divine commands, and consulting a scholar (alim) or jurist (imam) to know how to obey Allah does not mean taking them as the subject of obedience. 

• Necessity of Expertise: Deriving rules from the Qur'an and Sunna requires intensive study and mastery of Arabic and related sciences, which is impossible for every individual. Allah ordained in Qur'an 9:122 that a group should devote themselves to acquiring knowledge so others can consult them. 

• Essence of Taqlid: Taqlid is simply a person who cannot independently interpret the sources consulting a qualified jurist and acting upon their interpretation to fulfill the requirements of the Shari'a without committing shirk.

proofs.f: What is a madhhab ("school"), and how does following a particular school relate to following the Qur'an and Sunna?
proofs.b:
• Definition of Madhhab: A madhhab is a particular interpretation of the Shari'a and a collection of major shari' rules derived from the Holy Qur'an and Sunna by a reliable jurist, arranged subject-wise for the convenience of followers. 

• Relationship to Sources: The school of an Imam is not parallel or alien to the Shari'a; rather, someone who follows a particular school is actually following the Qur'an and Sunna according to the interpretation of a reliable, trustworthy jurist whom they believe is well-versed in matters of Shari'a.

proofs.f: What are the two types of rules mentioned in the Holy Qur'an and Sunna regarding interpretation, and what are the three main causes for differences of opinion among the various schools?
proofs.b:
• Two Types of Rules:

1. Clear rules allowing only one interpretation: Rules stated so clearly (such as prayer, zakat, fasting, pilgrimage, prohibition of pork and adultery) that all schools are unanimous, leaving no room for ijtihad, taqlid, or consulting an Imam. 

2. Rules allowing multiple interpretations: Rules derived where different situations or interpretations arise. 

• Three Causes for Differences of Opinion:

1. Wording with multiple interpretations: E.g., the word quru' in Qur'an 2:228 meaning either "menstruation" (Abu Hanifa رحمه الله) or "cleanliness/tuhr" (Shafi'i). 

2. Disparity between two hadiths: E.g., differing traditions regarding raising hands while bowing (ruku') in prayer. 

3. Unaddressed issues: Issues not specifically addressed in the Qur'an and Sunna, requiring solution through analogy (qiyas) or examples.

proofs.f: How do the schools of the four Imams compare to other schools, which school should a person follow, and how does the legal analogy of lower courts following a high court apply to madhhabs?
proofs.b:
• The Four Schools: While many jurists practiced ijtihad, the schools of the four Imams (Abu Hanifa رحمه الله, Malik, Shafi'i, Ahmad) became the most comprehensive, well-arranged, and well-preserved, and the Umma has taken them as having the most reliable interpretations. 

• Which School to Follow: All recognized schools are sincere and equally valid; a person should follow the school of any recognized Imam whom they believe to be most knowledgeable and pious. 

• Legal Analogy: Just as lower courts and citizens follow high court judgements (treating the high court as a trustworthy interpreter of the law, not a legislator), a Muslim following a jurist's school is following a trustworthy interpreter of the Shari'a, without accusing anyone of disregarding the law or committing shirk.

proofs.f: Why is "pick-and-mix" (talfiq) between different schools condemned for a non-professional layman, and how does it lead to following personal desires?
proofs.b:
• Following Desires over Evidence: A layman lacking the ability to compare arguments, if left free to choose any view, will naturally select views that fulfill personal convenience or desires rather than the strength of evidence—a practice condemned by the Qur'an. 

• Contradictory Combination Example: For instance, choosing the Hanafi view on touching a woman (doesn't break wudu') and the Shafi'i view on bleeding (doesn't break wudu') leaves a person acting upon a composite state that would be considered invalid by both schools combined. 

• Preventing Anarchy: The policy of allegiance to a single school (taqlid shakhsi) was adopted by jurists as a preventive measure to preclude anarchy in the Shari'a and stop people from treating the law as a plaything.

proofs.f: What are the exceptions where a person or qualified scholar may adopt a view from another madhhab?
proofs.b:
• Those Qualified in Ijtihad: Individuals equipped with the necessary qualifications of ijtihad do not need to follow a particular school and can derive rules directly from original sources. 

• Qualified Scholars / Experts: Those well-versed in Islamic disciplines who can evaluate different juristic views purely on academic grounds (without personal desires) are not forbidden from preferring one school over another in a specific matter. 

• Juristic Preference (Tarjih): Sometimes Hanafi jurists, after comprehensive study, conclude that another Imam's view is stronger based on evidence.

proofs.f: Why might jurists sometimes depart from the view of their own Imam, and what is required to adopt another school's view?
proofs.b:
• Grounds for Departure: Jurists may depart from their Imam's view if an analogy does not conform to an authentic hadith (which the Imam likely did not know of), or out of necessity for the collective good of the Umma in changing circumstances. 

• Conditions for Adopting Another View: Because all four schools rest on solid grounds, a competent scholar with the required knowledge, academic research capabilities, and freedom from personal desires may adopt another school's view. Those lacking these conditions must not do so to prevent legal anarchy.

proofs.f: Why does superficial self-study of translated texts lead to unjustified criticism of former jurists, and what does true extraction of juridical rules require?
proofs.b:
• Superficial Study Dangers: Individuals relying on cursory translation study often assume mastery and unjustifiably criticize former jurists out of ignorance. 

• Requirements for Rule Extraction: Extracting rules requires collecting scattered material across chapters, examining hadith veracity via usul al-hadith, studying historical backgrounds, and resolving complex issues—a level of intensive knowledge rarely found in contemporary non-specialists.

proofs.f: What is the definition of a tabi'i (Follower) according to the majority of hadith scholars, and how does Imam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله hold a unique status among the four Imams in this regard?
proofs.b:
• Definition: According to the majority of hadith scholars (preferred by Hafiz Ibn Hajar al-'Asqalani, Allama Iraqi, Ibn al-Salah, Nawawi, and Hakim), a tabi'i is someone who met a Companion (Sahabi) of the Messenger ﷺ or merely saw one while in a state of faith (iman). It is not necessary for him to have remained in their company or to have narrated from them. 

• Unique Status: Imam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله (born 80 A.H.) is confirmed by biographers and historians to be a tabi'i, having seen the Companion Anas ibn Malik رضي الله عنه ؓ multiple times when Anas رضي الله عنه visited Kufa. This is a unique rank held by him that cannot be said regarding the other three great Imams (Malik, Shafi'i, and Ahmad ibn Hanbal).

proofs.f: Which Companions (Sahaba) did Imam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله meet or narrate from, as recorded by scholars like Ibn Hajar al-Makki, Khatib al-Baghdadi, Daraqutni, and Imam 'Abd al-Qadir al-Misri?
proofs.b:
• Seeing Anas ibn Malik رضي الله عنه ؓ: Ibn Hajar al-Makki (al-Khayrat al-hisan), Khatib al-Baghdadi (Tarikh al-Baghdad), and Daraqutni (Tabyid al-sahifa) all confirm that Abu Hanifa رحمه الله saw Anas ibn Malik رضي الله عنه ؓ. 

• Companions Narrated From: According to Imam 'Abd al-Qadir al-Misri (al-Fawa'id al-bahiyya 42), the Companions from whom Abu Hanifa رحمه الله related hadiths include: 'Abdullah ibn Unays, 'Abdullah ibn Jaz'a al-Zabidi, Anas ibn Malik رضي الله عنه, Jabir ibn 'Abdullah رضي الله عنه, Ma'qil ibn Yasar, Wathila ibn al-Asqa', and 'A'isha رضي الله عنها bint 'l-Ajrad ؓ.

proofs.f: What account does Imam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله give regarding his meeting with the Companion 'Abdullah ibn al-Harith ibn Jaz'a ؓ during Hajj in 93 A.H.?
proofs.b:
• Imam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله relates that Abu Hanifa رحمه الله said he performed Hajj with his father in 93 A.H. when he was 16 years old. 

• He saw a crowd gathered around a teacher who his father identified as the Companion 'Abdullah ibn al-Harith ibn Jaz'a ؓ. 

• Abu Hanifa رحمه الله got close enough to hear him report that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever acquires an understanding of the religion of Allah, Allah suffices him in his matters of concern and provides him with sustenance from sources which he could not expect."

proofs.f: How do statements from scholars such as Hafiz al-Sam'ani, Makki ibn Ibrahim, 'Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, and Imam Shafi'i describe Imam Abu Hanifa's رحمه الله mastery of knowledge and status as a jurist?
proofs.b:
• Hafiz al-Sam'ani: Recounts that when visiting Abbasid caliph Mansur, 'Isa ibn Musa عليه السلام pointed to Abu Hanifa رحمه الله and declared, "This is the scholar of the world today" (al-Ansab 247). 

• Makki ibn Ibrahim (Shaykh of Imam Bukhari): Remembered him as the greatest scholar of his time (I'la' al-sunan 18:308). 

• 'Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak: Stated that when he inquired in Kufa about the most learned, devout, and knowledgeable person, scholars unanimously answered that it was Abu Hanifa رحمه الله, noting they knew of no one else possessing such characteristics (al-Mizan 58). He also remarked, "The greatest jurist is Abu Hanifa رحمه الله. I have not seen anyone like him in the field of jurisprudence". 

• Imam Shafi'i: Remarked that people are dependent on Abu Hanifa رحمه الله in the field of jurisprudence (Tahdhib al-Tahdhib 10:450), and when asked if Imam Malik met Abu Hanifa رحمه الله, Malik replied that he had seen a person who, if he said he could turn a pillar into gold, would be able to provide evidence for it (Tabyid al-sahifa 16).

proofs.f: How do scholars ('Allama Zafar 'Uthmani and Muhammad ibn Sama'a) explain Imam Abu Hanifa's رحمه الله extensive transmission and mastery of hadith?
proofs.b:
• Muhammad ibn Sama'a: States that the Imam mentioned more than 70,000 hadiths in his books and selected the Athar from 40,000 hadiths. 

• 'Allama Zafar 'Uthmani: Explains that all of the Imam's legal rulings (masa'il) are in actual fact hadiths narrated in the form of legal rulings rather than formal narrations. Furthermore, he compiled formal narrations through his personal chains that were collected in his students' Masanid and works (such as Imam Muhammad's رحمه الله Kitab al-athar, Muwatta, Hujaj; Abu Yusuf رحمه الله and Ibn al-Mubarak's works; Waki's Musnad; and collections by Ibn Abi Shayba, 'Abd al-Razzaq, Hakim, Ibn Hibban, Bayhaqi, and others). 

• Status as a Hadith Critic: Imam Dhahabi includes Imam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله in his Tadhkirat al-huffaz among those who possessed prophetic knowledge and could be consulted for their expertise in determining the authenticity or weakness of narrators.

proofs.f: How do statements from Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna, Imam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله, Mulla 'Ali al-Qari رضي الله عنه (describing the exchange with A'mash), and Ibn al-Mahdi highlight Imam Abu Hanifa's رحمه الله profound insight into hadith and evaluation of narrators?
proofs.b:
• Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna: Stated that the first person to encourage him to relate hadiths and make him a hadith scholar was Abu Hanifa رحمه الله. 

• Imam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله: Stated he never found anyone with more insight into the interpretation of hadiths than Abu Hanifa رحمه الله. 

• Mulla 'Ali al-Qari رضي الله عنه (Exchange with A'mash): When Abu Hanifa رحمه الله recited numerous extended chains of hadiths to A'mash from memory on the spot, A'mash exclaimed, "What took me a hundred days to narrate you repeated to me in just an instance... O group of jurists, you are the physicians, and we are merely the pharmacists". 

• Ibn al-Mahdi: Stated he never saw anyone possessing greater knowledge of the Sunna than Abu Hanifa رحمه الله, noting they only became aware of 'Amr ibn Dinar's agnomen (kunya) through him.

proofs.f: What is Ibn Khaldun's conclusive evaluation (Muqaddima) regarding the absurd claim that great jurists like Imam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله possessed only superficial knowledge of hadith?
proofs.b:
• Ibn Khaldun states that it is impossible for someone whom a vast majority of the Umma accepted as a competent jurist to possess only superficial knowledge of hadiths, because Islamic law can only be derived from the Qur'an and Sunna, requiring deep knowledge from the correct source. 

• The trust placed in Abu Hanifa's رحمه الله school throughout Islamic history establishes his greatness in the field of hadith.

proofs.f: How do Waki' ibn al-Jarrah and Asad ibn al-Furat describe the caliber of Imam Abu Hanifa's رحمه الله companions, students, and compilation of works?
proofs.b:
• Waki' ibn al-Jarrah (via Tarikh al-Baghdad): Defended Abu Hanifa رحمه الله by noting how absurd it is to claim he erred when he was surrounded by elite companions and sitting partners of immense caliber in analogy, inference, memorization, and Arabic language (such as Abu Yusuf رحمه الله, Zufar, Muhammad, Yahya ibn Zakariyya, Ibn Abi Za'ida, etc.) who would guide him to the truth. 

• Asad ibn al-Furat (via Imam Tahawi رحمه الله): Noted that the companions of Abu Hanifa رحمه الله who compiled and recorded his works numbered forty, with those in the forefront being Abu Yusuf رحمه الله, Zufar, Dawud al-Ta'i عليه السلام, Asad ibn 'Amr, Yusuf ibn Khalid al-Samti, and Yahya ibn Zakariyya ibn Abi Za'ida (who was his scribe for thirty years).

proofs.f: Why is Sayyidina 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud ؓ sometimes targeted with criticism, and what is his true standing among the Companions according to Ahl al-Sunna?
proofs.b:
• Reason for Attacks: Because many of his narrations form the basis of numerous opinions in the Hanafi school, some attempt to discredit the Hanafi school by attacking and criticizing this great Companion. 

• Standing and Status: The Companions are considered the most superior and exalted people after the Messengers, and no one after them can attain their status. 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud ؓ is one of the most revered Companions known for his deep understanding of the Qur'an and jurisprudence (fiqh).

proofs.f: What grave warnings did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ issue regarding criticizing or troubling his Companions?
proofs.b:
• Troubling Companions: The Prophet ﷺ stated that whoever loves them loves them out of love for him, and whoever hates them hates them out of hate for him. Whoever troubles them troubles Allah, and whoever troubles Allah, it is imminent that Allah will seize him (Mishkat al-Masabih, Tirmidhi 554). 

• Cursing Critics: The Prophet ﷺ instructed: "If you come across those who curse my Companions, say, 'May Allah's curse be upon you for your evil'" (Mishkat al-Masabih, Tirmidhi 554). 

• The Stars Metaphor: The Prophet ﷺ described his Companions as like the stars in the skies: "Some are stronger than others but each possesses a light. Whoever adopts any opinion from among the various opinions they differ in will be considered guided in My sight" (Mishkat al-Masabih, Razin al-'Abdari 554).

proofs.f: How did Hudhayfa رضي الله عنه ؓ describe 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud's ؓ resemblance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and what is signified by his agnomen "Ibn Ummi 'Abd"?
proofs.b:
• Resemblance: When asked who closely resembled the Messenger ﷺ in manner, conduct, and behavior, Hudhayfa رضي الله عنه ؓ replied: "We are not aware of anyone who possesses a closer resemblance to the Messenger ﷺ in manner, conduct, and habit than Ibn Ummi 'Abd" (Sahih al-Bukhari, Sunan al-Tirmidhi). 

• Agnomen Meaning: "Ummi 'Abd" was his mother's name, meaning that while Hudhayfa رضي الله عنه ؓ was not aware of his private life at home, his public social conduct perfectly mirrored that of the Messenger ﷺ.

proofs.f: How did Abu 'l-Darda' describe the status of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud ؓ to 'Alqama when they met in Syria?
proofs.b:
• Abu 'l-Darda' remarked: "Do you not have Ibn Ummi 'Abd among you, the keeper of the slippers and pillow of the Messenger ﷺ and the one in charge of his ablution water?" 

• He added that among them was also the one whom Allah protected from Satan, and the keeper of the Prophet's ﷺ secrets which no one else knew.

proofs.f: What did 'Umar ibn al-Khattab رضي الله عنه ؓ and 'Ali ibn Abi Talib رضي الله عنه ؓ state regarding 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud's ؓ profound knowledge and trustworthiness?
proofs.b:
• 'Umar ibn al-Khattab رضي الله عنه: Stated that whoever wants to recite the Qur'an as though it were freshly revealed should recite it according to Ibn Mas'ud's رضي الله عنه recitation. He also described him as "a small person brimming with [the knowledge of] jurisprudence". 

• 'Ali ibn Abi Talib رضي الله عنه: Stated, "If I were to appoint someone as a leader without consulting [anyone], I would appoint Ibn Ummi 'Abd". Furthermore, the Prophet ﷺ stated: "I am pleased for my Umma with whatever Ibn Ummi 'Abd is pleased with".

proofs.f: How do recommendations from the Prophet ﷺ, Mu'adh ibn Jabal رضي الله عنه ؓ, and Hudhayfa رضي الله عنه ؓ establish 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud ؓ as a premier source of knowledge?
proofs.b:
• The Prophet's ﷺ Directives: Instructed the Umma: "Learn [the knowledge] from four people: 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, Salim the slave of Abu Hudhayfa, Ubay ibn Ka'b, and Mu'adh ibn Jabal رضي الله عنه" (Sahih al-Bukhari, Sunan al-Tirmidhi). The Prophet ﷺ also commanded: "Whatever 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud narrates to you, accept it" (Sunan al-Tirmidhi). 

• Mu'adh ibn Jabal's رضي الله عنه Deathbed Advice: Advised people to take knowledge from four people, specifically including 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (Sunan al-Tirmidhi). 

• Hudhayfa's رضي الله عنه Statement: Stated that whatever Hudhayfa رضي الله عنه relates, accept it, but "however 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud teaches you to recite, recite in that way" (Sunan al-Tirmidhi).

proofs.f: How does 'Allama Dhahabi (Tadhkirat al-huffaz) describe the status, character, and caution in narration of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud ؓ?
proofs.b:
• Status and Titles: Described as the learned leader (al-imam al-rabbani), Abu 'Abd al-Rahman 'Abdullah ibn Ummi 'Abd al-Hudhali, personal servant and Companion of the Messenger ﷺ.

• Excellence: Among the first to embrace Islam, veterans of Badr, expert jurists, teachers of the Qur'an, and those who strove to convey the Prophet's ﷺ words accurately.

• Caution in Narration: Extremely scrupulous in his narrations, admonishing students who were negligent in recording exact words, and due to extreme caution, narrating very little himself, leading his students to never give preference to any Companion over him.

proofs.f: What is the spiritual consequence of criticizing or harboring enmity toward the Companions according to hadith and Qur'anic evidence?
proofs.b:
• Declaration of War (Divine Hadith): In a qudsi hadith (Sahih al-Bukhari), the Prophet ﷺ relates that Allah says: "Whoever harbors enmity towards a Friend (wali) of Mine, I declare war against him".

• Serious Crime: Belittling the position of any Companion—especially one endowed with so many virtues—is considered a very serious crime that incurs the wrath of Allah.

• Qur'anic Validation: Allah expresses His eternal pleasure with the Companions in Qur'an 9:100: "Allah is well pleased with them and they pleased with Him. He has prepared for them Gardens under which rivers flow...".

proofs.f: What are the common questions regarding foot distance in salat (prayer), and how do scholars generally address this issue?
proofs.b:
Common questions include: "How should I stand in prayer [salat]? Should I stand with my legs wide apart so that my feet touch those of the next person? Should I stand at my own comfort and not touch the feet of the next person? or Should I stand with a gap of four fingers between them as some people do?"

Discussions on this point by Islamic scholars are very few compared to other key prayer issues, making the precise views of even the four Imams quite difficult to determine.

proofs.f: What is the status of maintaining orderly rows in prayer, and what hadith emphasizes this warning?
proofs.b:
Having rows in perfect order is an important sunna (though not a fard/integral), and the imam is responsible for ensuring it before initiating prayer. Narrations carry warnings against disorderly rows, such as: 

"Straighten your rows, or else Allah will create discord between your hearts (Sunan Abi Dawud عليه السلام 1:97)".

proofs.f: How does the text analyze the hadith where Companions touched feet together in rows?
proofs.b: Upholders of spreading feet wide present a hadith where Companions touched feet together after being commanded to straighten rows. However, the text explains that this hadith does not in any way make joining the feet a wajib (necessary) act.

proofs.f: What are the two dominant opinions within the Hanafi school regarding foot positioning during prayer?
proofs.b:
1. Four-finger gap: Leaving a gap equal to four fingers of the hand. Radd al-muhtar (1:299) states: "The gap to be left between a person's feet should be equal to that of four fingers of the hand, because this [amount] is very effective in creating [the posture of] submission and humility [sought in prayer]". Jurists consider this superior because standing wide apart causes discomfort and loss of focus. 

2. Personal comfort / No stipulated distance: As noted in Ma'arif al-sunan (2:298), there is no mention in authentic hadith narrations of a stipulated space, so the sunna method is whatever distance a person finds convenient and comfortable while praying.

proofs.f: What is reported in Sunan al-Nasa'i regarding 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud and the meaning of murawaha?
proofs.b:
A hadith in Sunan al-Nasa'i (1:142) states: 

"'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud saw a person standing in prayer with his two feet together [i.e. touching each other] and judged it to be against the sunna. He advised the person that if he had practised murawaha it would have been more preferable". 

While murawaha can mean alternating weight between feet when tired, in this context it most probably means leaving a slight gap between the feet (instructing the person not to join them completely nor spread them too far apart).

proofs.f: What are the three recognized opinions of the Shafi'i school regarding the distance between the feet in prayer?
proofs.b:
1. A gap equivalent to one hand span between the feet (the most popular view, found in Nihayat al-muhtaj 1:347 U). 

2. A gap equal to four fingers (recommended in al-Anwar, common to both Shafi'i and Hanafi schools). 

3. As much of a gap as the person deems necessary (common to both Shafi'i and Hanafi schools). 

(Note: Imam Nawawi concludes in Sharh al-Muhadhdhab 3:266 U: "It is undesirable [makruh] to join the feet together; it is preferable [mustahab] to keep some distance between them.")

proofs.f: What is the full text of the hadith in Sunan Abi Dawud عليه السلام reported by Abu 'l-Qasim al-Jadali regarding joining feet and shoulders?
proofs.b: "I heard Nu'man ibn Bashir relate that the Messenger ﷺ faced the people and instructed, 'Straighten your rows. By Allah, you should straighten your rows or else Allah will create disagreement between your hearts.' Nu'man ibn Bashir ﷺ then said, 'I saw each person join his shoulders with those of the next person and his knees and ankles with those of the next person' (Sunan Abi Dawud عليه السلام 1:104)."

proofs.f: What key points show that the hadith of Nu'man ibn Bashir does not establish joining feet in salat as necessary (wajib)?
proofs.b:
1. The words describing the joining of feet are the narrator's observation of the Companions' reaction to the warning, not a direct command (marfu') from the Messenger ﷺ himself. The Messenger ﷺ merely commanded that lines be straightened. 

2. The narration describes the behavior of the Companions before the prayer began (prior to commencement to align the row) and does not indicate this posture was maintained throughout the prayer. 

3. Not a single juristic opinion in the major schools states that feet must be joined with those of the adjacent person.

proofs.f: What logical contradictions and practical difficulties arise if one assumes the joining of feet was maintained throughout the prayer?
proofs.b:
1. If required in all postures, joining feet/shoulders in prostration (sujud) or sitting (jalsa/tashahhud) would be practically impossible. 

2. If claimed only for standing (qiyam), maintaining this continuous contact throughout a row during standing is also extremely difficult. 

3. Knees were also mentioned as touching in the hadith of Sunan Abi Dawud عليه السلام; treating this as obligatory would be painful or impossible due to height and size differences between worshippers.

proofs.f: How did classical scholars like Hafiz Ibn Hajar and Imam Shawkani interpret the narration/chapter header regarding joining shoulders and feet?
proofs.b:
• Hafiz Ibn Hajar (Fath al-Bari 2:247): Explained that Imam Bukhari's chapter title ("Chapter on the Joining of the Shoulders and Feet Together While Forming the Rows") was used to exaggerate (mubalagha) the importance of straightening rows and filling gaps. 

• Imam Shawkani (Nayl al-awtar 3:65 U): Stated the phrase means placing body parts in line so each shoulder is in level with the next person's shoulder, forming a straight line, not that actual physical joining was an obligatory act.
