proofs.f: What statement did Anas رضي الله عنه ؓ make in Ma'mar's narration (Fath al-Bari 2:247) regarding joining shoulders and feet?
proofs.b:
"if I were to attempt this [joining the shoulders and feet together] with anybody today, they would scurry away like restive mules" (Fath al-Bari 2:247). 

Significance: Shows the Companions did not continue this physical practice as a permanent continuous sunna (sunna mustamirra) after the Prophet's ﷺ death.

proofs.f: Why is strict foot-joining unnecessary in modern masjids, according to point (7)?
proofs.b: Lines are clearly marked on carpets, marble, and floor coverings. Standing with heels aligned on the markings automatically forms perfectly straight rows without needing to force foot-to-foot contact.

proofs.f: Why is over-widening the feet (beyond shoulder width) during individual prayer ungrounded according to the text?
proofs.b:
1. If everyone in a row stood shoulder-to-shoulder, the gap between one's own feet could naturally only be as wide as the shoulders; spreading wider would make shoulder contact impossible. 

2. Hadiths describing Companions joining feet refer only to congregational alignment and cannot serve as evidence for widening feet during individual salat.

proofs.f: What is the author's final summary of the true sunna posture for foot placement in prayer?
proofs.b: The true sunna method is to leave a space of approximately four fingers between one's feet, or any gap that allows a comfortable and humble posture. In congregation, worshippers should stand close enough to touch shoulders while keeping heels on the row lines.

proofs.f: What differing positions of the hands do people observe when entering various masjids?
proofs.b: Some people stand in prayer with their hands clasped together beneath the navel, some folded on the chest, some just beneath the chest, and a few with their hands at their sides.

proofs.f: What are the two preliminary points clarified regarding the position of the hands in prayer?
proofs.b:
1. All positions mentioned in the hadiths are permissible, and the difference of opinion only concerns which is the most preferable method. 

2. There are very few rigorously authenticated (sahih) hadiths concerning this issue; most reports explaining the different ways have been classified as extremely weak or slightly defective.

proofs.f: What is the first difference of opinion concerning the positioning of the hands in prayer?
proofs.b: Whether the hands should be clasped together or not. Imam Malik's more popular opinion (related by Ibn al-Qasim) is that hands should be left hanging at the sides, while his second view (related by Ibn al-Mundhir) is that they should be brought together and placed on the body.

proofs.f: What is the consensus of the majority of scholars regarding whether hands should be clasped or left hanging at the sides?
proofs.b: Imam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله, Imam Shafi'i, Imam Ahmad, and the majority of scholars are of the opinion that the hands should be clasped together and not left to hang at the side. As the Maliki scholar Ibn 'Abd al-Barr states, there is nothing reported from the Messenger ﷺ contradicting this majority opinion, and it is the unanimous view of all Companions and Followers (tabi'in) (Awjaz al-masalik 2:116).

proofs.f: What reasons and reports exist regarding leaving the hands at the sides?
proofs.b: Scholars note there are no authentic hadiths substantiating Imam Malik's opinion of leaving hands at the sides. Some mention the reason may be profound fear, awe, and reverence for Allah causing a person standing before Him to forget bringing their hands together. Regardless, reports of some Companions praying with their hands on their sides can be found (Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba 2:391).

proofs.f: What is the second difference of opinion regarding the hands in prayer, and what are the specific views of the major imams?
proofs.b:
The difference is over where on the body hands should be positioned after clasping: 

• Imam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله and Abu Ishaq al-Marwazi (Shafi'i): Positioned below the navel. 

• Imam Shafi'i: Most popular view (in al-Wasit and Kitab al-Umm) is beneath the chest; a second opinion (in al-Hawi) is directly on the chest. 

• Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal: Three opinions—first (more popular, similar to Abu Hanifa رحمه الله) is beneath the navel; second is similar to Shafi'i (on the chest); third is that a person has the choice of either placing them beneath the navel or on the chest since both are derived from the Sunna.

proofs.f: Why is the narration of Wa'il ibn Hujr ؓ considered problematic (mudtarib) and inconsistent by scholars?
proofs.b:
Because different versions vary greatly on where the hands were placed: 

• Sahih Ibn Khuzayma: "I performed prayer with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He placed his right hand upon the left one on his chest." 

• Musnad al-Bazzar: States "near his chest" instead of "upon his chest". 

• Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba: States "beneath the navel." 

All three versions contain some type of weakness.

proofs.f: Why is the first version of Wa'il ibn Hujr's narration (found in Sahih Ibn Khuzayma containing "upon his chest") considered the weakest?
proofs.b:
• Mu'ammal ibn Isma'il: A weak narrator who erred after his books were buried and he narrated from memory. Imam Bukhari called him munkar al-hadith ("His narrations are rejected"), 'Allama Dhahabi said "He makes many errors" (kathir al-khata'), and Abu Zur'a noted his narrations contain many errors (Fath al-Mulhim 2:40). 

• Lack of corroboration: Other versions in Sunan Abi Dawud عليه السلام, Nasa'i, Ibn Maja, and Musnad Abi Dawud al-Tayalisi عليه السلام do not contain the addition "on the chest" (Allama Nimawi). 

• Broken link: Hafiz ibn Hajar al-'Asqalani stated the link between Mu'ammal and Sufyan al-Thawri is weak (Fath al-Bari 206 U). 

• Contradiction with narrator's view: Sufyan al-Thawri himself was of the opinion that hands should be positioned beneath the navel; under usul al-hadith, a narrator's narration in contradiction to his personal opinion is not accepted. 

• Not all of Ibn Khuzayma is authentic: Allama Suyuti noted in Tadrib al-rawi that Sahih Ibn Khuzayma contains some weak and munkar reports. 

• Imam Tirmidhi's silence: Tirmidhi made no comment regarding its authenticity, showing it is not rigorously authenticated. 

• Isolated practice (shadh): Even if accepted, placing hands on the chest would be considered an isolated practice done a few times solely to inform of its permissibility (bayanan li 'l-jawaz), not a permanent practice.

proofs.f: Why is the second version of Wa'il ibn Hujr's narration (found in Musnad al-Bazzar containing "near the chest") rejected?
proofs.b: One of its narrators is Muhammad ibn Hujr, regarding whom Imam Bukhari stated, "His matter is unsettled," and 'Allama Dhahabi stated, "Some of his narrations are rejected" (Majma' al-zawa'id 2:135).

proofs.f: What is the issue with the narration of Hulb ؓ transmitted by Imam Ahmad regarding placing the hand on the chest?
proofs.b: 'Allama Nimawi established with convincing evidence that there is a copyist error in the wording: instead of 'ala badhihi ("upon the other hand"), the copyist mistakenly wrote 'ala sadrihi ("on his chest") (Athar al-sunan 87).

proofs.f: What does the Hanafi explanation state regarding the various narrations of the Messenger ﷺ placing his hands on his chest or just below it?
proofs.b: The Hanafis explain that the Messenger ﷺ did, at one time or another, place his hands on his chest or just below it only to demonstrate the permissibility of such a posture (bayanan li 'l-jawaz), whereas his normal and routine practice was to place his hands below his navel.

proofs.f: What is the status of the third version of Wa'il ibn Hujr's narration mentioning "below the navel"?
proofs.b:
• Some Hanafi scholars noted it cannot be used as conclusive evidence because the words "below the navel" are only found in some editions of Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba (and not an inconsistent text). 

• However, 'Allama Qasim ibn Qutlubgah judged it to be of sound transmission, 'Allama Muhammad Abu 'l-Tayyib al-Madani wrote it has a strong chain, and Shaykh 'Abid Sindhi stated its narrators are trustworthy (Athar al-sunan 148). 

• Despite its problematic nature, it cannot be rendered totally unacceptable due to many other reliable reports strengthening it.

proofs.f: What is reported from 'Ali رضي الله عنه ؓ regarding placing hands below the navel, and what is the evaluation of its chain?
proofs.b:
• 'Ali رضي الله عنه ؓ stated: "To place one palm over the other beneath the navel is from the sunna acts of prayer" (Sunan al-Bayhaqi 312 U, Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba 1:391). 

• When a Companion says "It is from the Sunna," it is a known fact that it is acquired from the Messenger ﷺ himself. 

• The chain contains 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, who has been classified as weak; however, because other reliable narrations reinforce it, the Hanafis use it as supplementary evidence.

proofs.f: What are the narrations from Hajjaj ibn al-Hasan and Ibrahim al-Nakh'ay عليه السلام regarding hand placement?
proofs.b:
• Hajjaj ibn al-Hasan: Asked Abu Mijlaz about hand position, who replied: "He should place the inner portion of his right hand upon the back of the left one beneath the navel" (Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba 1:390), with a sound (hasan) transmission according to 'Allama Ibn al-Turkumani al-Mardini. 

• Ibrahim al-Nakh'ay عليه السلام: States "One should place his right hand upon the left one beneath the navel while in prayer" (Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba 1:390), also with a sound (hasan) transmission.

proofs.f: What are the reports from Abu Hurayra رضي الله عنه and Anas رضي الله عنه regarding hand placement beneath the navel?
proofs.b:
• Abu Hurayra رضي الله عنه: Narrates that "The placing of one hand over the other in prayer should be beneath the navel" (al-Jawhar al-naqi 2:31 U). 

• Anas رضي الله عنه: Reports that "there are three aspects from the characteristics of prophethood [nubuwwa]: to open fast early; to delay the predawn meal [suhur]; and to position the right hand over the left one beneath the navel while in prayer" (al-Jawhar al-naqi 2:31 U).

proofs.f: What reasoning does the great Hanafi jurist Ibn al-Humam provide for placing hands beneath the navel?
proofs.b: Due to inconsistencies and contradictions in various narrations, it is best to resort to analogy and reasoning. Standing before the Lord demands a posture expressing respect and reverence; positioning hands beneath the navel is the most respectful and superior way of standing. Additionally, women are instructed to place hands on their chests for greater concealment and modesty (Fath al-Qadir).

proofs.f: What does 'Allama Badr al-Din 'Ayni write in 'Umdat al-Qari regarding positioning hands beneath the navel?
proofs.b:
1. It holds great virtue, signifies great respect, and displays greater contrast to the postures of disbelievers. 

2. It is the same posture in which one stands before worldly rulers. 

3. Placing hands on the chest creates a similarity with women, hence it cannot be classified as the sunna for men ('Umdat al-Qari 3:16 U).

proofs.f: What is the chapter's final conclusion regarding hand placement in prayer?
proofs.b: Although hadiths from various schools contain some weakness, the Hanafi reports have received less criticism and have stronger reports to supplement weaker ones. Hadiths for placing hands on or below the chest do not denote the normal practice of the Messenger ﷺ, who Hanafis agree sometimes placed them on/below the chest only to show permissibility (bayanan li 'l-jawaz). Placing hands beneath the navel exhibits greater respect and humility, and just as other prayer postures differ between males and females, hand positioning differs as well.

proofs.f: Why is the issue of reciting behind the imam (qira'a khalF al-imam) considered so serious and controversial?
proofs.b: Because the debate is not just about which method is superior or more virtuous, but concerns the actual permissibility—whether reciting Surat al-Fatiha behind the imam is wajib (necessary) or totally forbidden (haram).

proofs.f: What points of agreement exist among scholars regarding recitation in prayer?
proofs.b:
1. All scholars agree that it is obligatory (fard) on the imam and the person praying by himself (munfarid) to recite Surat al-Fatiha. 

2. They agree the muqtadi (follower) is exempted from reciting anything beyond Surat al-Fatiha, whereas the imam and munfarid must recite at least a few short verses/small chapter in the first two rak'ats of fard prayers and all rak'ats of non-fard prayers.

proofs.f: What are the views of Imam Malik and Imam Ahmad regarding the follower reciting Surat al-Fatiha?
proofs.b: They are of the view that the follower is not required to recite Surat al-Fatiha in the audible (jahri) prayer, but is required to do so in the silent (sirri) prayers. Imam Malik stated it is undesirable (makruh) for the follower to recite in audible prayers (Fath al-Mulhim 2:20).

proofs.f: How did Imam Shafi'i's view on recitation behind the imam evolve between his popular view and his later book Al-Umm?
proofs.b:
• Popular/Former view: Necessary for the follower in both audible and silent prayers (al-Mughni 1:601). 

• Later view (Kitab al-Umm 7:153 U): Not necessary for the muqtadi to recite Surat al-Fatiha in audible prayers, but should be recited in silent prayers ("And we say that the follower should recite in every prayer performed behind an imam in which the imam recites in a non-audible tone"). (Confirmed as his later work by Hafiz Ibn Kathir and 'Allama Suyuti).

proofs.f: What is the view of Dawud al-Zahiri عليه السلام and Imam Ibn Taymiyya regarding reciting Surat al-Fatiha in audible prayers?
proofs.b: They were of the view that Surat al-Fatiha should not be recited in the audible prayers (making the view that it is fard in audible prayers an isolated and unique position).

proofs.f: What is the unanimous position of the Hanafi Imams (Abu Hanifa رحمه الله, Abu Yusuf رحمه الله, and Imam Muhammad رحمه الله) regarding recitation by the follower?
proofs.b: They state it is forbidden (haram)—though it does not nullify the prayer—for the follower to recite any portion of the Qur'an (whether Fatiha or another verse) in both silent and audible prayers behind the imam; the imam's recitation is sufficient for the follower.

proofs.f: What Qur'anic verse is presented as proof by the Hanafi school that no recitation should be undertaken by the follower?
proofs.b:
Allah says in the Qur'an:

"So, when the Qur'an is recited, listen to it, and remain silent, that you may receive mercy" (Al-Qur'an 7:204). 

The text notes this verse is sufficient proof that no recitation whatsoever should be...

proofs.f: According to Tanzim al-ashtat (commentary of Mishkat al-Masabih), what two commands does verse 7:204 give to the follower?
proofs.b:
1. To remain completely silent—which relates to both silent and audible prayers. 

2. To listen with concentration—which relates only to audible prayers.

proofs.f: How do Hafiz Ibn Taymiya and Imam Qudama (al-Mughni) counter the claim that verse 7:204 was revealed regarding the Friday sermon (khutba) only?
proofs.b:
• Ibn Taymiya: Pious predecessors (salaf salih) understood it was revealed concerning prayer (though some said sermon), and Imam Ahmad reported a consensus among scholars that it was revealed concerning prayer (Majmu' al-fatawa 23:269). 

• Imam Qudama: Imam Ahmad stated after a report of Abu Dawud, "The people are unanimous that this verse was revealed concerning the prayer" (1:601). Furthermore, it is a Makkan verse, whereas the Friday prayer and sermon only became obligatory later in Madina.

proofs.f: What narration is related from the great exegete Mujahid regarding the revelation of verse 7:204?
proofs.b: Both Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Imam Bayhaqi related a hadith from Mujahid that: "This verse was revealed concerning some Companions of the Messenger ﷺ reciting behind the imam". Even though it is mursal, Mujahid is known as a'lam al-nas bi 'l-tafsir (one of the greatest exegetes), so his mursal reports are accepted.

proofs.f: What report is related by Ibn Jarir al-Tabari from Yasir ibn Jabir regarding 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud ؓ?
proofs.b: 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud ؓ heard a few people reciting with the imam during prayer. Upon completing his prayer, he remarked: "Has the time not come for you to understand? Has the time not come for you to realize that when the Qur'an is being recited, you must listen to it attentively and remain silent just as Allah has ordered you to?" (I'la' al-sunan 4:43, Tafsir al-Tabari 11:378).

proofs.f: What is the Hanafi distinction between fard and wajib regarding obligations and the consequences of neglecting them?
proofs.b:
• Fard: Established through decisive proof (dalil qat'i); neglecting it renders the entire prayer invalid, and it cannot be compensated by prostrations of forgetfulness. 

• Wajib: Established through speculative proof (dalil zanni); neglecting it renders the prayer deficient (not entirely invalid) and can be compensated through the prostrations of forgetfulness (sajdat al-sahw).

proofs.f: How do the Hanafis derive that reciting any portion of the Qur'an is fard and reciting Surat al-Fatiha is wajib?
proofs.b:
• They derive that reciting any portion of the Qur'an is fard based on verse 73:20 ("So recite as much of the Qur'an as may be easy for you"), treating ma as a general ('am) term encompassing the whole Qur'an. 

• Based on the hadith "There is no prayer except with Surat al-Fatiha," they render the recital of Surat al-Fatiha specifically to be wajib. Thus, the imam and munfarid must recite Fatiha with other verses, while the muqtadi does not recite at all because they are commanded to remain silent.

proofs.f: What were the circumstances of revelation for verse 17:110 ("And say your prayer neither aloud nor in a low voice...") according to Ibn 'Abbas رضي الله عنهما ؓ?
proofs.b: It was revealed when the Messenger ﷺ was discreetly inviting people to Islam in Makka and recited aloud in prayer. When polytheistic mushrikin heard his recitation, they would revile the Holy Qur'an, Allah, and the Prophet ﷺ. Thus, Allah instructed: "And say your prayer neither aloud... but make it so that the believers can hear you" (Al-Ta'liq al-sabih 1:366, Sahih Muslim).

proofs.f: What are the full texts of Hadiths 1 and 2 (narrated by Abu Sa'id al-Khudri رضي الله عنه ؓ and Abu Hurayra رضي الله عنه ؓ) regarding remaining silent behind the imam?
proofs.b:
• Hadith 1 (Abu Sa'id al-Khudri ؓ): "The Messenger ﷺ delivered a sermon in which he outlined our Way [Sunna] for us and taught us our prayer. He instructed, 'When you prepare for prayer, straighten your rows; then one of you [should become the imam to] lead the others in prayer. When he proclaims the takbir you also proclaim it; when he recites remain silent; and when he reaches "ghayr al-maghdubi 'alayhim wala 'l-dallin," say "amin," and Allah will answer your prayer' (Sahih Muslim 1:174)". 

• Hadith 2 (Abu Hurayra ؓ): "The imam has been assigned to be followed. When he proclaims the takbir you also proclaim it; when he recites remain silent; and when he says "sami' Allahu liman hamidah," say "Rabbana laka 'l-hamd" (Sunan Abi Dawud عليه السلام 1:96, Sunan al-Nasa'i 46)".

proofs.f: What key deductions are drawn from Hadith 1 and 2 regarding amin and following the imam?
proofs.b:
1. Purpose of Amin: The follower says amin ("O Allah, accept") to endorse the du'a' made by the imam at the end of Fatiha. If followers were required to recite Fatiha themselves, they would say amin at the end of their own recitations, but the Prophet ﷺ ordered it said collectively upon the imam's completion. 

2. Meaning of "assigned to be followed": The follower must remain silent to listen to the imam's recitation; reciting on one's own while the imam recites would be rude and makes attentive listening impossible.

proofs.f: What are the narrations of Jabir رضي الله عنه ؓ and the Messenger ﷺ (Hadiths 3 & 4) regarding the sufficiency of the imam's recitation?
proofs.b:
• Jabir رضي الله عنه ؓ (Hadith 3): "whoever prays behind an imam, his imam's recitation is sufficient for him (al-Jawhar al-naqi 2:159, I'la' al-sunan 4:61, Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba 1:377)". 

• The Messenger ﷺ (Hadith 4): "Whoever prays behind the imam, his imam's recitation is sufficient for him ('Umdat al-qari 3:12, Muwatta Muhammad 96, I'la' al-sunan 4:61)".

proofs.f: What are the details of Hadith 5 ('Abdullah ibn Shaddad) and Hadith 6 regarding recitation behind the imam?
proofs.b:
• Hadith 5 ('Abdullah ibn Shaddad): The Messenger ﷺ led the 'Asr prayer. A person began reciting behind him, so the person next to him gave him a nudge. After finishing prayer, the person asked, "Why did you nudge me?" The other replied, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in front of you, and I did not approve of you reciting behind him." The Messenger ﷺ heard this and said, "Whoever has an imam, the recitation of the imam is sufficient for him" (Muwatta Imam Muhammad رحمه الله 98, I'la' al-sunan 4:70). 

• Hadith 6: Someone asked the Messenger ﷺ: "O Messenger of Allah ﷺ! Is there recitation in every prayer?" The Messenger ﷺ said yes. Somebody asked, "[Does that mean] it is necessary?" The Messenger ﷺ replied, "I consider the imam's recitation to be sufficient [for the muqtadi]" (Majma' al-zawa'id 2:110).

proofs.f: How does Ibn Taymiya summarize the legal ruling on the sufficiency of the imam's recitation in his Fatawa?
proofs.b: "The recitation of the imam is sufficient for the muqtadi. The consensus of the Companions and the Followers proves this. The hadiths from which this [rule] is established are narrated without any Companion being omitted from the transmission [musnadan], as well as some with the Companion being omitted from the transmission [mursalan]. The legal rulings [fatawa] among the Followers were also that the [imam's] recitation is sufficient. Above all, it is in total accordance with the Qur'an and Sunna (Majmu' al-fatawa 23:271)".

proofs.f: What is reported in Hadith 7 (Abu Hurayra ؓ), Hadith 8 ('Imran ibn Husayn ؓ), and Hadith 9 ('Abdullah ibn Mas'ud ؓ) regarding the Prophet's ﷺ disapproval of reciting behind him?
proofs.b:
• Hadith 7 (Abu Hurayra ؓ): After an audible salat, the Messenger ﷺ asked, "Did one of you recite with me?" A person replied, "Yes, O Messenger of Allah ﷺ." The Messenger ﷺ remarked, "I was wondering why I felt as if the words of the Qur'an were being taken from my tongue" (Sunan al-Tirmidhi 1:71, Muwatta Imam Malik 51, Sunan al-Nasa'i 1:146, Sunan Abi Dawud عليه السلام 1:146, Sunan Ibn Maja 61, Sunan al-Bayhaqi 2:157). Upon hearing this, people discontinued reciting behind him during audible prayers. 

• Hadith 8 ('Imran ibn Husayn ؓ): During Zuhr, a person recited Sabbihi isma rabbik al-a'la behind the Prophet ﷺ. Afterward, the Prophet ﷺ asked who recited it and remarked, "I thought one of you was taking it [the verses] from my tongue" (Sahih Muslim 1:172, I'la' al-sunan 4:56). 

• Hadith 9 ('Abdullah ibn Mas'ud ؓ): The Companions would recite behind the Messenger ﷺ. Once he said to them, "You have caused me confusion in my recitation of the Qur'an" (Majma' al-zawa'id 2:110, al-Jawhar al-naqi 1:162).

proofs.f: What are the reports from 'Ata' ibn Yasar and Nafi'/'Abdullah ibn 'Umar رضي الله عنهما regarding recitation behind the imam?
proofs.b:
• 'Ata' ibn Yasar: Enquired from Zayd ibn Thabit ؓ regarding recitation behind the imam; he said, "There is no recitation behind the imam" (Sahih Muslim 1:215). 

• Nafi' reporting from 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar رضي الله عنهما: When asked if anything should be recited behind the imam, he replied: "Whenever one of you prays behind the imam, the recitation of the imam is sufficient for him; but when you pray alone, you should recite for yourself." The narrator notes 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar رضي الله عنهما would not recite behind the imam (Muwatta Imam Malik 51, I'la' al-sunan 4:76).

proofs.f: What did 'Ubaydullah ibn Muqsim learn when he enquired from 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar رضي الله عنهما, Zayd ibn Thabit, and Jabir ibn 'Abdillah رضي الله عنه ؓ?
proofs.b: They informed him that there should be no recitation behind the imam in any prayer (Athar al-sunan 1:116, I'la' al-sunan 4:81).

proofs.f: How did 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud and Abu Jamra express their views on reciting behind the imam?
proofs.b:
• 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud: Expressed great disapproval, saying, "Would that the mouth of the person reciting behind the imam be filled with dust" (Athar al-sunan 1:116, I'la' al-sunan 4:81). 

• Abu Jamra: Asked Ibn 'Abbas رضي الله عنهما ؓ, "Should I recite when the imam is in front of me?" He said no (Athar al-sunan 1:116, I'la' al-sunan 4:81).

proofs.f: What did Ibn 'Abbas رضي الله عنهما ؓ narrate from the Messenger ﷺ regarding the imam's recitation?
proofs.b: That the recitation of the imam is sufficient for the muqtadi, whether he recites silently or aloud (Daraqutni 1:331, I'la' al-sunan 4:82).

proofs.f: What do the statements of Musa ibn 'Uqba عليه السلام, Musa ibn Sa'id عليه السلام, Ibrahim al-Nakh'ay عليه السلام, and Muhammad ibn Sirin state regarding recitation behind the imam?
proofs.b:
• Musa ibn 'Uqba عليه السلام: Reports that the Messenger ﷺ, Abu Bakr رضي الله عنه, 'Umar رضي الله عنه, and 'Uthman رضي الله عنه would forbid reciting behind the imam (Umdat al-qari 3:67 U, I'la' al-sunan 4:84). 

• Musa ibn Sa'id ibn Zayd ibn Thabit عليه السلام (from Zayd ibn Thabit): "Whoever recites behind the imam, there is no prayer for him" (Muwatta Imam Muhammad رحمه الله 100, I'la' al-sunan 4:87). 

• Ibrahim al-Nakh'ay عليه السلام: "The first thing the people innovated [in religion] was recitation behind the imam—the Companions did not recite behind the imam" (al-Jawhar al-naqi 4:169). 

• Muhammad ibn Sirin: "I do not consider reciting behind the imam to be from the Sunna" (Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba 1:377, I'la' al-sunan 4:90).

proofs.f: Which ten Companions are reported by 'Abdullah ibn Zayd ibn Aslam to have strongly prohibited reciting behind the imam?
proofs.b: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq رضي الله عنه, 'Umar al-Faruq رضي الله عنه, 'Uthman ibn 'Affan رضي الله عنه, 'Ali ibn Abi Talib رضي الله عنه, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf رضي الله عنه, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas رضي الله عنه, 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, Zayd ibn Thabit, 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar رضي الله عنهما, and 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas (Qala'id al-azhar 2:42 U).

proofs.f: What statements were made by 'Ali ibn Abi Talib رضي الله عنه ؓ, Sa'd ؓ, and 'Umar رضي الله عنه ؓ regarding the invalidity or prohibition of reciting behind the imam?
proofs.b:
• 'Ali ibn Abi Talib رضي الله عنه: "Whoever recites behind the imam, his prayer is not valid," and in another narration: "[...] such a person has deviated from the natural path [fitra]" (al-Jawhar al-naqi 2:218, Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba 1:376). 

• Sa'd: "I desire that a burning ember be placed in the mouth of one who recites behind the imam" (Musannaf 'Abd al-Razzaq 2:138, Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba 2:376). 

• 'Umar رضي الله عنه: "Would that there be a stone in the mouth of one who recites behind the imam" (Musannaf 'Abd al-Razzaq 2:128).

proofs.f: What are the four primary reasons/rationales provided for not reciting behind the imam?
proofs.b:
1. Concentration & Audible Recitation: The imam recites aloud so followers listen in total silence; if followers recited as well, they could not concentrate on the imam's recitation, forcing the imam to recite aloud to a congregation not required to listen. 

2. Representation in Du'a': Surat al-Fatiha contains a du'a' (invocation for guidance); just as a group appointing a single representative to speak or submit a proposal does so without interference from members, the imam makes the du'a' on behalf of the entire congregation, who endorse it by saying amin. 

3. Late Arrivals in Ruku': If someone arrives late and joins the imam directly in bowing (ruku'), they still acquire that rak'a even though they missed the standing posture (qiyam) and reciting Fatiha, proving Fatiha is not fard on the muqtadi since the imam's recitation is sufficient. 

4. Congregational Commonalities: When an imam makes a mistake, the whole congregation performs sajdat al-sahw with him; when he recites a "verse of prostration," the congregation performs sajda even if recited silently; a single sutra in front of the imam is sufficient for the whole congregation. Thus, the imam's recitation being sufficient follows this same communal principle.

proofs.f: What are the two narrations of 'Ubada ibn al-Samit regarding recitation in prayer, and how do scholars generally view them?
proofs.b:
• Narrations: 1) "There is no prayer for the one who does not recite Surat al-Fatiha" (Sahih Muslim); 2) "There is no prayer for the one who does not recite Surat al-Fatiha and [some] more [verses]" (Sahih Muslim). 

• Status: Classified as rigorously authenticated (sahih), they are typically presented as evidence that reciting Fatiha is fard on the muqtadi.

proofs.f: What are the five explanations (a–e) provided by scholars/Hanafi texts to reconcile 'Ubada ibn al-Samit's narration with the Hanafi position?
proofs.b:
(a) Both imam and muqtadi are obligated, but the follower's obligation is fulfilled through the imam's recitation since the Messenger ﷺ stated the imam's recitation is sufficient for the muqtadi. 

(b) The hadith concerns the imam and the person praying by himself only, as followers are commanded in the Qur'an to remain silent and listen. 

(c) Rigorously authenticated hadiths totally prohibit the follower from reciting behind the imam; thus, in view of those prohibitions, this hadith is directed at the imam and lone worshipper. 

(d) The second narration includes "and more" (fasa'idan). Since everyone agrees that reciting extra verses is not fard on the follower (its obligation being absolved by the imam's recitation), the exact same reasoning applies to Surat al-Fatiha. 

(e) The obligation of Surat al-Fatiha is directed at the imam and the person praying alone only.

proofs.f: What statement of Jabir رضي الله عنه ؓ with a reliable transmission is narrated in Sunan al-Tirmidhi (1:71)?
proofs.b:
"Whoever performed a rak'a in which he did not recite Surat al-Fatiha, is as though he has not performed it, unless he was [praying] behind the imam" (Sunan al-Tirmidhi 1:71). 

Explanation: Imam Tirmidhi noted Imam Ahmad explained that Jabir رضي الله عنه (a Companion) interpreted the general statement to apply only when praying by oneself.

proofs.f: What are the details of the second narration of 'Ubada ibn al-Samit regarding the Fajr prayer (Sunan Abi Dawud عليه السلام, Tirmidhi, Nasa'i)?
proofs.b: During Fajr behind the Messenger ﷺ, the Prophet ﷺ experienced difficulty reciting. Upon finishing, he asked, "Perhaps you were reciting behind your imam?" When they replied yes, he said, "Do not recite anything besides Surat al-Fatiha, for there is no prayer for the one who does not recite it". A narration in Sunan Abi Dawud عليه السلام adds: "I was wondering why the words of the Qur'an were being taken from my tongue. Do not recite any portion of the Qur'an while I am reciting aloud, except Surat al-Fatiha".

proofs.f: Why do scholars state that the apparent wording allowing Fatiha in the second narration cannot be taken literally or is set aside?
proofs.b:
(a) Weak narrator in chain: Muhammad ibn Ishaq is present; while some considered him trustworthy, major critics like Sulayman al-Taymi عليه السلام, Hisham, and Imam Malik called him a "flagrant liar" (kadhdhab / dajjalun min al-dajajila), alongside severe criticisms from Ibn Zahir, Daraqutni, and others. 

(b) Confusion in transmission (mudtarib): Makhul relates it sometimes from Muhammad ibn Rabi', sometimes from Nafi' ibn Mahmud (whom experts like Ibn 'Abd al-Barr, Tahawi, and Ibn Qudama state is "unknown" / majhul). 

(c) Defective (ma'lul / mu'allal): Hadith experts classified it as defective because its transmission reached only 'Ubada ibn al-Samit (mawquf) rather than the Prophet ﷺ (marfu'), as explained by Ibn Taymiya and Imam Ahmad.

proofs.f: What further explanation does Imam Tirmidhi give regarding the transmission of 'Ubada ibn al-Samit's narration about Fajr prayer?
proofs.b: Imam Tirmidhi notes that the actual authenticated (sahih) narration of the Messenger ﷺ in this regard is simply "There is no prayer without the Umm al-Quran," transmitted in Sahihayn via Zuhri from 'Ubada ؓ through Muhammad ibn Rabi'. However, some narrators from al-Sham (Levant) erred, as 'Ubada ؓ was the Imam of Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) when he related this, and they confused his own statement (mawquf) as being related directly from the Messenger ﷺ (marfu'). Thus, the addition is inadmissible as evidence.

proofs.f: How do Hanafis interpret the phrase "iqra' ha fi nafsik" ("recite it in your mind") from Abu Hurayra's رضي الله عنه narration?
proofs.b:
1. It means "recite it in your mind and ponder over it, and do not utter it with your tongue," allowing the muqtadi to concentrate on the imam's recitation. 

2. It could be translated as "Recite it when you are performing prayer individually," supported by a hadith qudsi stating: "If the servant remembers Me while he is alone [fi nafsi], I remember him similarly [fi nafsi]; and if he remembers Me in a gathering, then I remember him in a gathering more superior to his". Since the opposite of being in a gathering is being alone, the meaning is to recite Surat al-Fatiha when praying alone, not in congregation.

proofs.f: What virtue and ruling are associated with saying amin after Surat al-Fatiha, and what does the hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari (1:108) state?
proofs.b:
• Virtue & Ruling: Saying amin ("aameen") holds great virtue and is a sunna of the Prophet ﷺ; all scholars are unanimous that it is sunna to say it at that time. 

• Hadith (Sahih al-Bukhari 1:108): "When the imam says 'ghayr al-maghdubi 'alayhim wala 'l-dallin,' say amin, because the angels say amin. And whoever's amin coincides with the amin of the angels, all his past sins are forgiven".

proofs.f: What is the nature of the difference of opinion regarding saying amin audibly or silently, according to Ibn al-Qayyim (Zad al-ma'ad 1:70)?
proofs.b: The difference of opinion is solely about which method is superior (audible vs. silent). Ibn al-Qayyim notes it is among valid differences where no criticism should be directed at those who say it aloud or silently, comparing it to the issue of raising hands (raf' al-yadayn).

proofs.f: What are the different opinions of the schools regarding whether amin should be said audibly or silently?
proofs.b:
• Hanafi Opinion: Amin should be said inaudibly at all times; the Prophet ﷺ said it aloud only a few times to familiarize Companions, after which he said it silently like all other invocations. 

• Another Group: Should be said aloud in all audible prayers (Fajr, Maghrib, 'Isha) and silently in silent prayers (Zuhr, 'Asr). 

• Imam Malik and Imam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله: The imam should say amin silently in silent prayers, and followers should always say amin silently in both audible and silent prayers (an opinion also shared by Imam Shafi'i). 

• Another Group: Followers should say amin audibly during audible prayers and silently during silent prayers. 

(Note: Saying amin aloud or silently is regarded by all as a sunna act, not a fard).

proofs.f: How do scholars explain that amin is a du'a (invocation), referencing Sura Yunus عليه السلام (10:89) and 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah (Sahih al-Bukhari 1:102)?
proofs.b:
• Definition: Amin is a verbal noun meaning "accept [our] prayer," making it a du'a. 

• Sura Yunus عليه السلام (10:89): Regarding "Accepted is your prayer (O Musa عليه السلام and Harun)!," the dual tense ("da'watukuma") is used even though only Musa عليه السلام made the du'a and Harun endorsed it with amin. Ibn Mardawayh relates via Anas رضي الله عنه that Musa عليه السلام made the du'a and Harun said amin (Fath al-Bari). 

• 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah: Quoted by Imam Bukhari in Sahih al-Bukhari (1:102) as saying, "Amin is a du'a". 

• Etiquette: Since it is a du'a, it follows the etiquette taught by Allah: "Invoke your Lord with humility and in secret. He likes not the aggressors" (Al-Qur'an 7:55).

proofs.f: How do Qur'anic verses (e.g., 13:3, 21:90, 20:108) support the position that amin should be said silently?
proofs.b:
• Allah commands making prayers and du'as with humility, sincerity, and in silence (khufya). 

• Zakariyya's invocation was "a call in secret" (13:3). 

• Envoys "used to call on Us with hope and fear" (21:90). 

• On the Last Day, "you shall hear nothing but the low sound of their footsteps" (20:108). 

Since amin is a du'a, it should be said silently like other du'as, matching the teachings that Allah is Near and All-Hearing and does not require loud invocation.

proofs.f: What is mentioned in the narration of Samura ibn Jundub and 'Imran ibn Husayn ؓ regarding the Prophet's ﷺ silences (sakta)?
proofs.b:
• Samura related two occasions of short silence in prayer: one following the initial takbir and the second when completing wala 'l-dallin. 

• 'Imran ibn Husayn initially wrote to Ubay bin Ka'b because he couldn't acknowledge this; Ubay replied that Samura remembered correctly (Sunan Abi Dawud عليه السلام 1:120). 

• Commenting on this, 'Allama Nimawi states the first silence was to recite thana silently, and the second was to say amin silently. 'Imran likely refuted the second silence because it was so brief and he didn't think it worthy of mention, acknowledging the longer first silence. This proves amin was recited during the second silence (Athar al-sunan 382).

proofs.f: How does the narration of Abu Hurayra رضي الله عنه ؓ (Sunan al-Nasa'i 1:147) indicate that the imam should say amin silently?
proofs.b: The Prophet ﷺ instructed: "When the imam recites 'ghayr al-maghdubi 'alayhim wala 'l-dallin,' say amin, because the angels say it and so does the imam". If it were preferable for the imam to say it aloud, there would be no reason for the Prophet ﷺ to inform the Companions that the imam also says amin, because they would have heard it themselves. Informing them means it was normally said in a subdued tone.

proofs.f: What are the two differing reports from Shu'ba and Sufyan al-Thawri regarding Wa'il ibn Hujr's ؓ narration about saying amin?
proofs.b:
• Shu'ba's narration: When the Prophet ﷺ reached wala 'l-dallin, he said amin and kept his voice subdued (Musnad Ahmad, Daraqutni, al-Mustadrak U, Nasb al-raya 1:494). 

• Sufyan's narration: The Prophet ﷺ prolonged his voice (madda biha sawtahu) while saying amin (Sunan al-Tirmidhi 1:57, Abi Dawud عليه السلام 1:142). 

• Hanafi/Scholarly Reconciling: While critics favor Sufyan's report to claim amin was said aloud, Hanafis explain that Sufyan's report means the initial vowel (alif) of amin was prolonged (elongated) rather than the volume of the voice being raised, a position supported and defended in works like Athar al-sunan and Fath al-Mulhim.

proofs.f: How do Hanafis interpret Abu Hurayra's رضي الله عنه narration ("When the imam says amin, you say it") (Sahih al-Bukhari 1:108)?
proofs.b: If it were preferable to say amin aloud, the wording would have read "When the imam says amin, you say it" using the imam's audible amin as the direct signal. However, because the Prophet ﷺ instructed them to say amin after the imam recited wala 'l-dallin, it shows the imam's amin was pronounced silently. Occasional narrations saying "When the imam says amin..." are interpreted as "When the time comes for the imam to say amin..." rather than literally, since his normal practice was to say it silently.

proofs.f: What do the reports from early Companions and Followers (Abu Wa'il, Ibrahim al-Nakh'ay عليه السلام) state regarding bismillah, ta'awwudh, and amin?
proofs.b:
• Abu Wa'il: 'Ali رضي الله عنه and 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud ؓ did not recite bismillah, a'udhu bi'llah, or amin aloud (Majma' al-zawa'id 2:108); 'Umar رضي الله عنه and 'Ali رضي الله عنه ؓ would also not recite them aloud (I'la' al-sunan 2:215). 

• Ibrahim al-Nakh'ay عليه السلام (Musannaf 'Abd al-Razzaq 2:87): Stated there are five things the imam should say silently: subhanaka 'llahumma (thana), ta'awwudh, bismillah, amin, and Allahumma rabbana laka 'l-hamd.

proofs.f: What additional reasons are provided for saying amin silently?
proofs.b:
1. Avoiding Confusion with the Qur'an: Quranic recitation must be audible in audible prayers; saying amin aloud could mislead people into assuming it is part of the Qur'an alongside Fatiha, whereas all scholars agree amin is not part of the Qur'an. 

2. Analogy to Bismillah: Some scholars consider bismillah a verse of Surat al-Fatiha yet do not recite it aloud during prayer, proving that invocations like amin (which no scholar considers part of the Qur'an) should definitely not be said aloud.

proofs.f: How do Hanafis answer the narration of Abu Hurayra رضي الله عنه (Sunan Abi Dawud عليه السلام) stating that amin was heard in the first row, including the version in Sunan Ibn Maja (1:61) about the masjid echoing?
proofs.b:
1. Weak narrator: One of its narrators is Bishr ibn Rafi', who has been strongly criticized by hadith experts—Imam Bukhari stated "He is not consistent in his narrations," Imam Ahmad called him weak, Imam Nasa'i stated "He is not strong," and Ibn Hibban stated "He relates spurious narrations" (Mizan al-i'tidal U). 

2. Self-contradictory: It is unclear how one version states it was heard from the first row only, while the other states the whole masjid echoed. Thus, the hadith is self-contradictory and cannot be accepted as evidence.

proofs.f: How do scholars (like Ibn al-Qayyim, Ibn Jarir al-Tabari, and Hafiz Abu Bishr al-Dulabi) reconcile the differing reports regarding saying amin aloud vs. silently?
proofs.b:
• General reconciliation: The Prophet ﷺ said amin aloud only for a short period of time to emphasize its importance and teach the Companions, similar to 'Umar رضي الله عنه reciting thana aloud for a few days before continuing silently, or 'Abbas reciting Fatiha during funeral prayer to teach it (Zad al-ma'ad 1:70). 

• Wa'il ibn Hujr's statement: Transmitted by Hafiz Abu Bishr al-Dulabi: "I do not think the Messenger ﷺ said it [amin] aloud except to teach us" (Athar al-sunan 93, Fath al-Mulhim 2:50-52). 

• Ibn Jarir al-Tabari: Both types of reports are reliable/authentic (sahih), referring to different occasions—silent reports reflect his normal, permanent practice, while audible reports reflect rare instances to teach the Companions.

proofs.f: What points are raised regarding the frequency of prayer and the scarcity of reports supporting audible amin?
proofs.b: There are five prayers a day. If amin were said aloud in three of them permanently, it would have been widely reported by many Companions rather than just a few. Wa'il ibn Hujr, who lived in Yemen, visited Madinah only a few times, so the Prophet ﷺ likely said it aloud in his presence solely to teach him (as Wa'il himself noted: "I do not think the Messenger ﷺ said it aloud except to teach us"). Furthermore, Wa'il's narration in Sunan al-Nasa'i (1:147 U) states: "When the Messenger ﷺ recited 'ghayr al-maghdubi 'alayhim wala 'l-dallin,' he said amin. I heard him [say it] since I was behind him," indicating he only heard it because he was directly behind him, not because it was pronounced loudly.

proofs.f: What is the nature of the difference of opinion regarding raising the hands (raf' al-yadayn) in prayer, and is it a matter of fard or haram?
proofs.b: It is not a debate about something being obligatory (fard) or unlawful (haram), but merely a difference in ascertaining the better of two ways (which method is more virtuous). Both methods are permissible according to most scholars, as both are derived from hadiths.

proofs.f: What are the three main positions regarding raising the hands at various points in the prayer?
proofs.b:
1. Opening takbir (tahrima): All scholars are unanimous that hands should be raised at this point. 

2. Before and after bowing (ruku'): One group states it is sunna and more virtuous to raise hands; another group (including Imam Malik and Imam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله) holds that it is sunna and preferable not to raise hands at these instances. 

3. Moving into prostration (sajda) or returning to third standing (qiyam): All scholars of Ahl al-Sunna are unanimous that it is no longer sunna to raise hands at these instances, as that practice was abrogated.

proofs.f: What regional practices (ta'amul) of the three great early Islamic cities (Madina, Makka, and Kufa) shaped the juristic views on raf' al-yadayn?
proofs.b:
• Madina (Imam Malik): Based his opinion on the continuous practice of the people of Madina who did not observe raising the hands after the opening takbir. As stated in al-Mudawwana: "I do not consider the raising of the hands to be part of any takbir of the prayer... except at the beginning of prayer" (al-Mudawwanat al-kubra 1:71). 

• Makka (Imam Shafi'i): Based on the practice of the inhabitants of Makka following the teachings of 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr ؓ, favoring raising the hands. 

• Kufa (Imam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله): Influenced by 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud and 'Ali رضي الله عنه ؓ (who moved the caliphate to Kufa) alongside approximately 1,500 Companions. As Muhammad ibn Nasr al-Marwazi noted (quoted by 'Allama 'Iraqi in Sharh al-Taqrib): "We are not aware of any city, in which all its inhabitants had completely abandoned the practice of raising the hands at all instances of ascending or descending in prayer, besides the people of Kufa" (Ithaf al-sadat al-muttaqin 3:54).

proofs.f: What remarks did Imam Tirmidhi make regarding the chapters on raising vs. not raising the hands in his Sunan?
proofs.b:
• At the end of the chapter on raising hands, he remarked: "This is the opinion of a few [ba'd] Companions".

• At the end of the chapter on not raising hands, he remarked: "This is the opinion of more than one [ghayru wahidin]" (indicating a greater number than ba'd).

These remarks indicate that the practice of not raising the hands was very widespread.

proofs.f: What are the three types of hadiths regarding raf' al-yadayn categorized in the text?
proofs.b:
1. Those clearly mentioning that the Messenger ﷺ raised his hands at the time of ruku'.

2. Those mentioning that the Messenger ﷺ never raised his hands except when uttering the opening takbir.

3. Those describing the complete prayer of the Messenger ﷺ but not mentioning whether or not he raised his hands after the opening takbir.

proofs.f: How do Hanafi scholars use the third category of hadiths (those not mentioning hand raising) alongside the second category?
proofs.b:
• Not mentioning something only evidences that it was not a popular practice.

• If raising hands had been an important, regular aspect of prayer, a narrator describing the complete prayer could not have failed to mention it.

• Furthermore, not raising hands is a "nonexistent" action, and people do not mention nonexistent actions in conversation (comparable to someone arriving home without an accident, where nobody remarks "He did not fall").

• Thus, when combined with the second category, hadiths supporting not raising hands actually outnumber those in support of it.

proofs.f: What are the seven instances within salat where hadiths report the Messenger ﷺ raising his hands at one time or another?
proofs.b: (1) At the initial takbir; (2) before and after bowing (ruku'); (3) before descending into prostration (sajda); (4) between the two prostrations (sujud); (5) when beginning the second rak'a; (6) when beginning the third rak'a; (7) at the change of every new posture in prayer.

proofs.f: Why do proponents of raising hands (group one) adopt only the first two instances (opening takbir and ruku') and abandon the rest?
proofs.b: Whatever reason group one has for adopting only two instances and abandoning the rest serves as the same reason for Imam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله and Imam Malik to adopt the first instance only and abandon the others.

proofs.f: What are the primary sources of evidence for group one versus the Hanafi school regarding raf' al-yadayn?
proofs.b:
• Group One: Primarily rely on narrations of Ibn 'Umar رضي الله عنهما and Malik ibn al-Huwayrith ؓ (who reported raising hands at all seven instances, though group one accepted only opening takbir and ruku').

• Hanafi School: Rely on reports whose narrators are consistent, primarily the narrations of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud ؓ, who states that hands were raised at the initial takbir only and not repeated at any other time in the prayer.

proofs.f: How did Imam Malik view the narrations of Ibn 'Umar رضي الله عنهما ؓ regarding raising hands, given his famous "golden chain" (silsilat al-dhahab)?
proofs.b: Although Imam Malik received many narrations from Ibn 'Umar رضي الله عنهما via Nafi' (his famous "golden chain"), he did not base his opinion on them for this issue; instead, he adopted the narrations of Ibn Mas'ud رضي الله عنه ؓ and gave preference to the continuous practice (ta'amul) of the people of Madina, which was to raise hands at the initial takbir only.

proofs.f: What inconsistencies are noted in some narrations of Ibn 'Umar رضي الله عنهما ؓ regarding raising hands?
proofs.b: In one narration mentioned in Imam Tahawi's رحمه الله Mushkil al-athar, it states that the hands were raised at every movement of the prayer, whereas in his other narrations, this is not mentioned. This confusion prevents his inconsistent reports from being adopted over more precise and consistent ones.

proofs.f: What are the details of the first narration of 'Alqama reporting from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud ؓ concerning raf' al-yadayn?
proofs.b:
• 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud ؓ said: "Should I not demonstrate the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for you?" He performed the prayer, and did not raise his hands except at the initial takbir (Sunan al-Tirmidhi 1:59, Sunan al-Nasa'i 1:161, Sunan Abi Dawud عليه السلام 1:116). 

• Imam Tirmidhi classifies this hadith as sound (hasan), 'Allama ibn Hazm classifies it as rigorously authenticated (sahih) (al-Muhalla 4:88), and 'Allama Ahmad Muhammad Shakir defended its authenticity against criticism.

proofs.f: What do 'Alqama's second and third reports from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud ؓ state regarding the Prophet's ﷺ hand-raising?
proofs.b:
• Second Report: The Messenger ﷺ stood up and raised his hands at the outset and did not do so again (Sunan al-Nasa'i 1:158, I'la' al-sunan 3:48). 

• Third Report: The Messenger ﷺ would raise his hands at the opening takbir, then would not raise them again (Sharh Ma'ani 'l-athar 224).

proofs.f: What statement does 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud ؓ make in his fourth report regarding the early Caliphs?
proofs.b: "I prayed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abu Bakr رضي الله عنه, and 'Umar رضي الله عنه ؓ. They did not raise their hands except at the beginning of prayer" (Nasb al-raya 1:526, Majma' al-zawa'id 2:101).

proofs.f: What do the narrations of Salim from his father (Ibn 'Umar رضي الله عنهما ؓ) (such as in Sahih Ibn 'Awana 2:90 U) confirm regarding hand-raising?
proofs.b: Ibn 'Umar رضي الله عنهما ؓ stated that when beginning prayer, the Messenger ﷺ would raise his hands to shoulder level and thereafter would not raise them again before or after bowing, nor between the two prostrations (sujud). This confirms the Messenger ﷺ did not raise his hands at the time of ruku', a report also transmitted by Imam Humaydi in his Musnad via a rigorous chain.

proofs.f: What do 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas and Ibn 'Umar رضي الله عنهما ؓ report regarding seven instances where hands are to be raised (Nasb al-raya 1:521)?
proofs.b: The hands are to be raised at: (1) the beginning of prayer, (2) when setting sight on the House of Allah, (3) at Safa, (4) Marwa, (5) 'Arafat, (6) Muzdalifa, and (7) when saluting the [black] stone. Notably, there is no mention of raising hands at the time of bowing (ruku').

proofs.f: What is narrated by Jabir ibn Samura رضي الله عنه ؓ regarding the prohibition of raising hands, and how do Hanafis interpret it?
proofs.b:
• Narration: The Messenger ﷺ approached and remarked, "Why is it that I see you raising your hands as though they are the tails of restive horses? Remain calm in prayer" (Sahih Muslim 1:181, Sunan al-Nasa'i 1:176, Sunan Abi Dawud عليه السلام 1:150).

• Interpretation: The Prophet ﷺ prohibited raising hands while performing prayer (during ruku', prostration, etc.). This cannot apply to the opening takbir, since raising hands then is outside the formal actions of prayer (tahrima) and does not interfere with the prescribed calmness (sukoon).

proofs.f: How do scholars distinguish Jabir ibn Samura's رضي الله عنه narration about "tails of restive horses" from the separate narration concerning salam?
proofs.b:
Some mistakenly claim the hadith refers to making salam at the end of prayer. However, comparing the circumstances proves they are two separate incidents:

1. In Jabir's رضي الله عنه narration, Companions were engrossed in prayer when addressed, whereas the salam narration involves gesturing when making salam.

2. Jabir's رضي الله عنه narration prohibits "raising hands during prayer" and instructs calmness in prayer, whereas the salam narration prohibits gesturing right and left with hands when making salam.

3. The wording explicitly uses "in prayer," whereas salam is made at the conclusion of prayer.

proofs.f: What do the two narrations of 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas ؓ (reports 9 and 10) state regarding hand placement outside of prayer?
proofs.b: The hands should not be raised except at seven instances: at the beginning of prayer, when entering Masjid al-Haram and setting sight on the House of Allah, when standing on Safa, Marwa, 'Arafat, Muzdalifa, and (in report 10) when pelting the jamarat (Nasb al-raya 1:290 U, Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba 1:237).

proofs.f: What does Bara' ibn 'Azib ؓ report regarding the Messenger's ﷺ hand-raising in prayer (reports 11 and 12)?
proofs.b:
• Ibn Abi Layla report: Observed the Messenger ﷺ raise his hands at the initial takbir when beginning prayer (Daraqutni 1:293), and Ibn Abi Layla himself was known not to raise his hands thereafter (Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba 1:237). 

• Bara' ibn 'Azib report: When the Messenger ﷺ would begin prayer, he would raise his hands up to his ears, then not do so again. One version adds "only once," and another adds "then he would not raise them again until completing the prayer" (Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba 1:236, Sunan Abi Dawud عليه السلام 1:109 U).

proofs.f: What do the reports from Aswad, 'Abd al-Malik, 'Asim ibn Kulayb (from 'Ali رضي الله عنه ؓ), and Ibrahim al-Nakh'ay عليه السلام state regarding Companions and Followers?
proofs.b:
• Aswad: Performed prayer with 'Umar رضي الله عنه ؓ and observed him raise his hands only when beginning prayer (Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba 1:237). 

• 'Abd al-Malik: Observed that Sha'bi, Ibrahim al-Nakh'ay عليه السلام, and Abu Ishaq did not raise their hands except at the beginning of prayer (Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba 1:237). 

• 'Asim ibn Kulayb (from his father, companion of 'Ali رضي الله عنه ؓ): 'Ali رضي الله عنه would raise his hands only at the initial takbir when beginning prayer; thereafter, he would not raise them again at any other place (Muwatta Imam Muhammad رحمه الله 94, Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba 1:236). 

• Ibrahim al-Nakh'ay عليه السلام: 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud ؓ would raise his hands at the beginning of prayer, then would not raise them again (Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba 1:236).

proofs.f: What do the reports from Mujahid, Imam Malik (via Abu Hurayra رضي الله عنه ؓ), and Abu Ishaq state?
proofs.b:
• Mujahid: Did not see 'Umar رضي الله عنه ؓ raise his hands except at the beginning of prayer (Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba 1:236). 

• Imam Malik (from Na'im ibn 'Abdallah al-Mujmir and Abu Ja'far al-Qari): Abu Hurayra رضي الله عنه ؓ would lead them in prayer, saying the takbir every time he moved from one posture to another, but would raise his hands when saying the takbir at the beginning of the prayer [only] (Muwatta Imam Muhammad رحمه الله 90). 

• Abu Ishaq: The companions of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud and 'Ali رضي الله عنه ؓ would not raise their hands except at the beginning of prayer; Waki' confirms they would not raise them thereafter (Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba 1:236).

proofs.f: What conclusion is drawn from the list of Companions and Followers who did not raise their hands?
proofs.b: Abu Bakr رضي الله عنه, 'Umar رضي الله عنه, 'Ali رضي الله عنه, Ibn Mas'ud رضي الله عنه, Ibn 'Umar رضي الله عنهما, Abu Hurayra رضي الله عنه, and many other Companions, followed by Sha'bi, Ibrahim al-Nakh'ay عليه السلام, Abu Ishaq, Qays, Aswad, 'Alqama, and Ibn Abi Layla, all did not raise their hands except at the initial takbir. They would not have omitted raising hands at ruku' had it been the regular practice of the Messenger ﷺ.

proofs.f: How do Qur'anic verses on khushu' (humility) and qunut (devoutness) (2:2; 2:238) relate to the reasoning for not raising the hands?
proofs.b:
• 2:3:2: "Successful indeed are the believers, those who humble themselves [khashi'un] in their prayers". 

• 2:2:238: "Stand before Allah in a devout frame of mind [qanitin]". 

Both humility (khushu') and calmness are required in salat. Because the Prophet ﷺ prohibited raising hands due to interference with calmness (resembling tails of restive horses), not raising the hands maintains this prescribed stillness and devout frame of mind.

proofs.f: How do Hanafi scholars apply the principle of naskh (abrogation) to the issue of raising hands at ruku'?
proofs.b: Whenever naskh occurred regarding a prayer action, it always concerned an action that was initially commanded and practiced, since nonexistent practices cannot be abrogated (just as early talking/moving in prayer were initially permitted and later abrogated). Thus, raising hands at ruku' was initially allowed and later abrogated, leaving only the opening takbir. Furthermore, hadiths prohibiting raising hands (e.g., Jabir ibn Samura's رضي الله عنه narration) are consistent and preferred over inconsistent ones, and narrators who report hand-raising (like Ibn 'Umar رضي الله عنهما) have themselves been reported not to raise their hands, whereas the primary narrator of non-raising, Ibn Mas'ud رضي الله عنه, never deviated from his consistent reports.

proofs.f: What points are made regarding the juristic rank (fiqh) and age/proximity of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud ؓ compared to Ibn 'Umar رضي الله عنهما ؓ?
proofs.b:
• Juristic Rank: 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud was a greater jurist than Ibn 'Umar رضي الله عنهما, and Ibn Mas'ud's رضي الله عنه students ('Alqama and Aswad) were greater jurists than Nafi' (who reported from Ibn 'Umar رضي الله عنهما); hence, by usul al-hadith, Ibn Mas'ud's رضي الله عنه narrations are preferred. 

• Age & Proximity: Ibn Mas'ud رضي الله عنه was older than Ibn 'Umar رضي الله عنهما, giving him more opportunity to stand in the first row closer to the Messenger ﷺ for a clearer view, whereas Ibn 'Umar's رضي الله عنهما youth meant he did not stand in the front rows. Moreover, Ibn Mas'ud رضي الله عنه enjoyed an exceptionally close relationship as a personal servant and teacher of the Qur'an who was extremely scrupulous in his narrations.

proofs.f: What incidents are related by Mughira ibn Muqsim and Urwa ibn Murra regarding Ibrahim al-Nakh'ay عليه السلام and 'Alqama ibn Wa'il?
proofs.b:
• Mughira ibn Muqsim: Mentioned Wa'il ibn Hujr's hadith of raising hands to Ibrahim al-Nakh'ay عليه السلام, who responded: "If Wa'il has seen the Messenger ﷺ raising his hands once, then Ibn Mas'ud رضي الله عنه ؓ has seen him fifty times not raising them" (Sharh Ma'ani 'l-athar). 

• Urwa ibn Murra: Entering the mosque of Hadhramaut, he heard 'Alqama ibn Wa'il narrate hand-raising from his father. When mentioning this to Ibrahim al-Nakh'ay عليه السلام, Ibrahim عليه السلام responded angrily: "Is Wa'il ibn Hujr the only one to have seen the Messenger ﷺ? Did not Ibn Mas'ud رضي الله عنه ؓ and his companions also see him?" (Muwatta Imam Muhammad رحمه الله 92).

proofs.f: How does the presence of physical body motions in prayer support the allocation of hand-raising to the opening takbir?
proofs.b: All other invocations in prayer are accompanied by a specific body motion (e.g., takbir before bowing, tasmi' when returning, takbir before prostration). Since there is no accompanying body motion for the beginning and ending of prayer, raising hands was allocated to the opening takbir (and turning the head for taslim). If hands were raised at ruku', the takbir and tasmi' would be accompanied by two actions (bowing down and raising hands), violating the standard of having only one motion per invocation.

proofs.f: What is the chapter's final conclusion regarding raf' al-yadayn before and after bowing?
proofs.b: Hadiths mentioning hand-raising at ruku' do not establish it as a permanent practice (sunna mustamirra); rather, raising hands before and after bowing is a sunna matruka ("an earlier practice of Allah's Messenger ﷺ which he later abandoned"). Hanafis acknowledge the Prophet ﷺ raised his hands at various instances, but as a temporary practice, with regular raising restricted to the opening takbir (while a weak/fabricated narration of Ibn 'Umar رضي الله عنهما claiming lifelong practice contains fabricators like 'Isma ibn Muhammad and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Quraysh).

proofs.f: What are the definitions and physical descriptions of the tawarruk and iftirash sitting postures in prayer?
proofs.b:
• Tawarruk: When a person sits with the left posterior on the ground; his right foot placed vertically with toes pointing towards the qibla; and the left foot on its side emerging from under the right foot. 

• Iftirash: Placing the left foot on its side and sitting on it; and keeping the right foot vertical, while resting on the bottom of the toes, turning them toward the qibla.

proofs.f: What are the four different group opinions regarding when to use iftirash versus tawarruk in the sittings of prayer?
proofs.b:
1. Hanafi view: The more superior and preferred method is to use iftirash in all sittings of the prayer, though sitting in tawarruk is also permissible based on sahih hadiths. 

2. Second group: More preferable to use tawarruk in all sittings of the prayer. 

3. Third group: More preferable to use iftirash in the first sitting and tawarruk in the "final" one (meaning a 2-rak'a prayer uses tawarruk for its only sitting). 

4. Fourth group: Use iftirash in the "first" sitting of every prayer and tawarruk in the second (so a 2-rak'a prayer uses iftirash, while 3 or 4-rak'a prayers use iftirash for the first sitting and tawarruk for the second sitting).

proofs.f: How does the Hanafi school explain the occasions when the Messenger ﷺ used tawarruk?
proofs.b: The Hanafis state the Prophet ﷺ sat in iftirash for the greater part of his life in all sittings. The few times he did tawarruk was either due to physical weakness/age making it difficult to sit in iftirash in the latter part of his life, or merely to inform the Companions of its permissibility (bayanan li 'l-jawaz).

proofs.f: What do the narrations from 'Aisha رضي الله عنها ؓ and 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar رضي الله عنهما ؓ (Sahih Muslim, Sahih al-Bukhari, Sunan al-Nasa'i) state regarding iftirash?
proofs.b:
• 'Aisha رضي الله عنها ؓ: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would spread his left foot and keep the right one standing" (Sahih Muslim 1:195). 

• 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar رضي الله عنهما ؓ: "It is a sunna of prayer that you keep your right foot standing and fold the left one" (Sahih al-Bukhari 1:114); and "among the sunnats of prayer is that you keep the right foot standing with the toes pointed towards the qibla, and [that you] sit on the left foot" (Sunan al-Nasa'i 1:173). 

• Wa'il ibn Hujr ؓ: "I came to Madina to observe the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ prayer. When he sat for tashahhud, he spread his left foot and kept the right one standing" (Sunan al-Tirmidhi 1:65, classified as sahih and noted by Tirmidhi as the practice of the majority, Sufyan al-Thawri, Ibn al-Mubarak, and the people of Kufa).

proofs.f: How do scholars reason that iftirash entails more reward based on difficulty, quoting 'Aisha رضي الله عنها ؓ?
proofs.b: Iftirash is slightly more difficult than tawarruk, and the more difficult a form of worship, the more reward it entails. As 'Aisha رضي الله عنها ؓ relates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The reward is in proportion to the hardship [you undertake]" (Sahih al-Bukhari, Muslim).

proofs.f: How do Hanafis and scholars respond to narrations describing the Messenger ﷺ or companions sitting in tawarruk or cross-legged (tarabbu' SY)?
proofs.b:
1. Weakness/Age: The Prophet ﷺ or Ibn 'Umar رضي الله عنهما adopted tawarruk or cross-legged sitting due to physical weakness, pain, or difficulty in their legs/advanced age during their final years, as confirmed by Ibn 'Umar's رضي الله عنهما statement ("My legs do not support me") (Sharh Ma'ani 'l-athar, Sahih al-Bukhari). 

2. Permissibility (Bayanan li 'l-jawaz): Used on rare occasions simply to demonstrate that sitting in tawarruk or cross-legged is permissible and not unlawful. 

3. Action vs. Verbal Command (Hadith Fi'li vs. Qawli): Tawarruk narrations describe an action (hadith fi'li), whereas iftirash is supported by explicit verbal commands (ahadith qawliyya), which take precedence in usul al-hadith. 

4. Reconciliation: Abu Humayd al-Sa'idi narrated both postures because his later narration highlighted the Prophet's ﷺ practice in his final years due to weakness, while his general/earlier narrations establish iftirash as the regular, continuous practice.

proofs.f: What is the final conclusion of the chapter regarding the sitting postures in prayer?
proofs.b: Both iftirash and tawarruk are found in the hadith literature and both are permissible, so a person has the choice of sitting in either position. However, because the Messenger ﷺ used iftirash for most of his life and as his continuous practice (confirmed by Ibn 'Umar رضي الله عنهما), sitting in iftirash is more virtuous and rewarding, while recourse to tawarruk is made in the event of inability or weakness.

proofs.f: What importance and virtues are attributed to the sunna prayer of Fajr in the hadiths of 'Aisha رضي الله عنها ؓ and Abu Hurayra رضي الله عنه ؓ?
proofs.b:
• 'Aisha رضي الله عنها ؓ (Sahih Muslim 1:251): The Prophet ﷺ was more regular and hastened towards the two rak'ats before Fajr than any other supererogatory (nafl) prayer, stating: "They are more superior than the world and everything within it" / "They are more beloved to me than the entire world". 

• Abu Hurayra رضي الله عنه ؓ (Sunan Abi Dawud عليه السلام 1:186, Athar al-sunan 1:224): "Do not abandon the sunna rak'ats of Fajr, even if horses trample over you".

proofs.f: What is the general rule regarding performing sunna prayers once the iqama has been called (Sahih Muslim 1:247)?
proofs.b: The Messenger ﷺ stated: "Once the call to commence [iqama] is made for the prayer, there is no prayer except the fard prayer [maktuba]". Thus, once congregational fard prayer begins, no other sunna prayer is permissible in other prayers.

proofs.f: What is the dilemma when a person arrives late for Fajr and finds the congregational prayer about to begin or in progress, and what are the differing opinions?
proofs.b:
• Dilemma: Balancing the extreme emphasis on the Fajr sunna against the rule prohibiting sunna prayers once iqama or fard begins. 

• Opinion 1: Immediately join the congregation for fard, as performing sunna during congregational fard is no longer permissible (ruling for other prayers). 

• Imam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله & Imam Malik: Attempt to perform the sunna prayer if confident of completing it quickly and joining the fard before it ends (even if catching only the last sitting), provided one is confident of not missing the congregation completely; otherwise, abandon sunna and join the congregation. 

• Additional Hanafi View: Only attempt the sunna if confident of acquiring at least one rak'a behind the imam (certain of catching him before he stands up from ruku' of the second rak'a of fard). 

(Note: If performed after the fard prayer has begun, the Fajr sunna should be done outside the main prayer-hall/masjid area where the congregation is in progress).

proofs.f: What do the reports from Nafi', Abu Ishaq, Abu 'Uthman al-Ansari, and Imam Tahawi رحمه الله (regarding Abu 'l-Darda') state about Companions performing the Fajr sunna when joining late?
proofs.b:
• Ibn 'Umar رضي الله عنهما (via Nafi'): Awakened when prayer had commenced, he arose and performed the two rak'ats (sunna first) (Sharh Ma'ani 'l-athar 1:375).

• 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud: Arriving when congregation had begun, he positioned himself behind a pillar in the masjid and performed two rak'ats sunna first, then joined the congregation (Sharh Ma'ani 'l-athar 1:374).

• 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas: Arrived while the imam was leading Fajr; since he had not yet performed the two rak'ats sunna, he performed them behind the imam (separately), then joined the congregation (Sharh Ma'ani 'l-athar 1:375).

• Abu 'l-Darda': Would enter the masjid while everybody was in rows performing Fajr, perform his two rak'ats in a corner of the masjid, then join the fard prayer (Sharh Ma'ani 'l-athar 1:375).

proofs.f: What do the reports from Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi, Haritha ibn Mudrib, Abu 'l-Darda', Ibn 'Umar رضي الله عنهما, Sha'bi (regarding Masruq), and Hasan al-Basri state?
proofs.b:
• 'Umar ibn al-Khattab رضي الله عنه (via Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi): When congregation had already started, they would first perform their two rak'ats at the rear of the masjid, then join the congregation (Sharh Ma'ani 'l-athar 1:376).

• Haritha ibn Mudrib: 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud and Abu Musa رضي الله عنه left Sa'id ibn al-'As; congregation had begun, so Ibn Mas'ud رضي الله عنه performed two rak'ats sunna first, while Abu Musa رضي الله عنه joined the row immediately (Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba 2:251).

• Abu 'l-Darda': If he entered and found everyone in prayer, he would go to a pillar and perform two rak'ats quickly, then join the congregation (Musannaf 'Abd al-Razzaq 1:443; also noted in another report).

• Ibn 'Umar رضي الله عنهما: Sometimes joined immediately, and at other times would first perform his two rak'ats at one side of the masjid (Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba 2:251).

• Masruq (via Sha'bi): Entered to find people in Fajr prayer; since he had not performed the two rak'ats sunna, he performed them at one side, then joined the congregation (Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba 2:251, Musannaf 'Abd al-Razzaq 2:444).

• Hasan al-Basri: Instructed that when you enter the masjid and find the imam in prayer and have not yet performed the two rak'ats of Fajr, perform them first, then join the imam in the fard prayer (Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba 2:445, Sharh Ma'ani 'l-athar 1:376).

proofs.f: What are the four reasons / arguments provided in support of the Hanafi opinion regarding performing the Fajr sunna late?
proofs.b:
1. Greater Emphasis: The emphasis on the sunna of Fajr is far greater than any other sunna prayer (ordered to be performed even if horses trample over the person), excluding it from the general prohibition once congregation begins.

2. Lengthy Recitation in Fajr: Fajr fard involves a lengthy recitation of the Qur'an, making it feasible to quickly perform the two rak'ats sunna and still join the imam during the first rak'a, second rak'a, or just before the salam (unlike other prayers with shorter recitations and four rak'ats).

3. Non-General Command: The command prohibiting non-fard prayers when congregation begins is not an absolute general command encompassing all situations (analogous to how scholars permit performing sunna prayers at home even after knowing congregation has begun in the masjid).

4. Meaning of "Maktuba": The word maktuba in the hadith includes missed (qada') prayers, indicating missed prayers can be performed even after congregation has begun; thus the command is not taken literally in an absolute sense.

proofs.f: What are the three main issues regarding witr prayer that the chapter focuses on?
proofs.b: (1) How many rak'ats is the witr prayer? (2) How many salams in the witr prayer? (3) Is performing one rak'a sufficient for witr?

proofs.f: What are the varying opinions of the schools regarding the number of rak'ats and structure of witr?
proofs.b:
• Imam Shafi'i: Witr can be performed in units of one, three, five, seven, nine, or eleven rak'ats. (Though some Shafi'is differentiate between Ramadan vs. other months, or congregation vs. individual).

• Imam Ahmad: Odd rak'ats ranging from one to eleven; main view is performing witr as one rak'a preceded by qiyam al-layl.

• Imam Malik: Recommends at least three rak'ats; does not recommend a single rak'a for witr.

• Imam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله: Witr should be performed as three continuous rak'ats with two sittings (one in the second rak'a and the other in the third) with salams to be performed in the final sitting only.

proofs.f: What did 'Aisha رضي الله عنها ؓ report regarding the Prophet's ﷺ night and witr prayer (Sahih al-Bukhari, Sahih Muslim)?
proofs.b:
• The Prophet ﷺ would not perform more than eleven rak'ats (neither in Ramadan nor out of it): performing four rak'ats (of great beauty and length), followed by another four, and then performing three [witr].

• When asked if he slept before performing witr, he replied: "O 'Aisha رضي الله عنها! My eyes sleep, but my heart does not".

proofs.f: What does Sa'id ibn Hisham relate from 'Aisha رضي الله عنها ؓ regarding the structure of the three rak'ats of witr (Sunan al-Nasa'i, Muwatta Imam Muhammad رحمه الله)?
proofs.b: 'Aisha رضي الله عنها ؓ informed him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not make salams in the second rak'a of witr.

proofs.f: What do the narrations of Imam Hakim (al-Mustadrak 1:304) and Sa'id ibn Hisham state regarding making salams in witr?
proofs.b:
• Imam Hakim / 'Aisha رضي الله عنها: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would not make salams in the first two rak'ats of witr (al-Mustadrak 1:304); he would perform three rak'ats of witr making salams only at the end (in the final rak'a), which was also the practice of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab رضي الله عنه and the people of Madina. 

• Sa'id ibn Hisham (Musnad Ahmad 6:156 U): After 'Isha, the Prophet ﷺ would perform sets of two rak'ats, and thereafter perform the witr prayer without any interval in between (i.e., without salams in the second rak'a).

proofs.f: How do scholars explain narrations mentioning numbers like "four with three, six with three, or eight with three" (Sunan Abi Dawud عليه السلام 1:200)?
proofs.b: The whole tahajjud prayer has been described as witr, whereas in reality only three rak'ats were witr, and the remaining four, six, or eight rak'ats were tahajjud. Umm al-mu'minin 'Aisha رضي الله عنها distinguished between the three rak'ats of witr and the various other rak'ats.

proofs.f: What surahs did the Prophet ﷺ recite in the three rak'ats of witr according to 'Aisha رضي الله عنها ؓ and Ibn 'Abbas رضي الله عنهما (Sunan Abi Dawud عليه السلام, Tirmidhi, Nasa'i, etc.)?
proofs.b:
• First rak'a: Sabbih isma rabbika al-a'la [Surat al-A'la]. 

• Second rak'a: Qul ya ayyuha 'l-kafirun [Surat al-Kafirun]. 

• Third rak'a: Qul huwallahu ahad [Surat al-Ikhlas] along with the Mu'awwadhatayn [Surat al-Falaq and al-Nas]. (Declared sound [hasan] by Imam Tirmidhi, and authenticated by Imam Hakim and 'Allama Dhahabi).

proofs.f: Which other Companions are listed as narrating or supporting that witr consists of three rak'ats concluded with salams only at the end?
proofs.b: (1) 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza, (2) Ubay ibn Ka'b, (3) 'Ali ibn Abi Talib رضي الله عنه, (4) 'Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa, (5) 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, (6) Nu'man ibn Bashir, (7) Abu Hurayra رضي الله عنه, (8) 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar رضي الله عنهما, (9) 'Imran ibn Husayn, (10) Abu Khaythama (via his father Mu'awiya ibn Khadij), and (11) Anas ibn Malik رضي الله عنه (via Thabit al-Bunani, noting it was acquired from Jibril عليه السلام from Allah).

proofs.f: What reports from Miswar ibn Makhrama, 'Umar ibn al-Khattab رضي الله عنه, Hasan al-Basri, and 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud confirm the practice of three rak'ats with one set of salams?
proofs.b:
• Miswar ibn Makhrama: After burying Abu Bakr رضي الله عنه, 'Umar رضي الله عنه remembered he hadn't performed witr; he led them in three rak'ats and made salams only at the end in the third rak'a (Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba 2:293 U). 

• 'Umar ibn al-Khattab رضي الله عنه: Stated he would not neglect the three rak'ats of witr even for red camels (Muwatta Imam Muhammad رحمه الله 150), and performed them without intermediate salams (Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba 2:295). 

• Hasan al-Basri: Informed that 'Umar's رضي الله عنه practice was to stand up for the third without making salams after the second, noted 'Umar رضي الله عنه was a greater jurist (al-Mustadrak 1:304). 

• 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud: Stated the rak'ats of witr are three, similar to the daytime witr prayer (i.e., Maghrib) (Muwatta Imam Muhammad رحمه الله 150), and explicitly stated that one rak'a does not suffice for witr (Muwatta Imam Muhammad رحمه الله 150).

proofs.f: What do the reports from Anas رضي الله عنه, Ibn 'Abbas رضي الله عنهما, Ubay ibn Ka'b, Abu Umama, and others state concerning the number of rak'ats in witr?
proofs.b:
• Anas رضي الله عنه (Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba 2:293): Witr is three rak'ats. 

• Ibn 'Abbas رضي الله عنهما (via Abu Mansur and 'Ata'): Stated witr is three rak'ats and is similar to the Maghrib prayer (Sharh Ma'ani 'l-athar, Muwatta Imam Muhammad رحمه الله 150). 

• Ubay ibn Ka'b (via Hasan al-Basri): Would perform three rak'ats for witr and would make salams only at the end of the third rak'a (Musannaf 'Abd al-Razzaq 2:294). 

• Abu Umama (via Abu Ghalib): Would perform three rak'ats for witr (Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba 2:294). 

• Alqama: Stated witr is three rak'ats (Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba 2:294). 

• Ibrahim al-Nakh'ay عليه السلام: Stated there is no witr consisting of less than three rak'ats (Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba 2:294). 

• Umar ibn 'Abd al-Aziz رضي الله عنه: Designated the rak'ats of witr to be three based on the ruling of the jurists, with salams to be made only at the end (Sharh Ma'ani 'l-athar). 

• Hasan al-Basri: Stated that the Muslims have reached a consensus (ijma') concerning witr being three rak'ats with salams only at the end (Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba 2:294).

proofs.f: What is the consensus among the prominent Companions, Followers, and the Fuqaha' Sab'a regarding witr?
proofs.b: Prominent Companions like 'Umar رضي الله عنه, 'Ali رضي الله عنه, Ibn Mas'ud رضي الله عنه, Ibn 'Umar رضي الله عنهما, Anas رضي الله عنه, Ibn 'Abbas رضي الله عنهما, 'Aisha رضي الله عنها, Ubay ibn Ka'b, and Abu Umama all stated in clear terms that witr consists of three rak'ats. Subsequent Followers (Ibrahim al-Nakh'ay, 'Alqama, Abu Ishaq, Qasim ibn Muhammad) and the fuqaha' sab'a ("the seven great jurists") also concluded that witr was three rak'ats, leading Hasan al-Basri to report consensus (ijma') on this.

proofs.f: What are the two differing opinions regarding the number of salams in the witr prayer?
proofs.b:
1. Hanafi Opinion: Like every other prayer, only one set of salams should be made in witr, concluding at the end of the third rak'a without performing two sets of salams that would perform the third rak'a separately. 

2. Other Scholars' Opinion: The person praying (musalli) should first perform two rak'ats, terminate them with salams, and then perform the third rak'a separately with another set of salams.
